## AgentIdentity

`kardinal.io/v1alpha1`

AgentIdentity registers an AI agent: the principals that are the agent, the person who answers for it, where it may act and how far on its own.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object | yes | AgentIdentitySpec registers an agent (docs/actors.md). |
| `spec.autonomy` | string |  | Autonomy is the agent's ceiling: auto, approve (a person approves its promotions) or deny. A Pipeline environment can only tighten it. One of: `auto`, `approve`, `deny`. Default: `approve`. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions` | []object |  | BudgetExemptions are break-glass exceptions to the budgets. One made by an agent, or without an actor stamp, never counts. Planned: added with kardinal override --budget (W7, #2438) by someone the cluster lets exempt the agent, never of the agent's own party (W6, #2437). |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].actor` | object |  | Actor is who made the exception, stamped as on freeze exemptions. An exemption whose actor is an agent, or that has none, is never honoured: break-glass is for people (docs/design/24-agent-budgets.md section 11.3). Planned (W6, #2437): the chart's actor admission policy verifies it from the requester's username and groups. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].actor.asserted.client` | string |  | Client is the tool that wrote the record (for example kardinal/0.12.0). |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].actor.asserted.model` | string |  | Model is the AI model the client says it runs. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].actor.asserted.session` | string |  | Session is the client's session or run identifier. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].actor.kind` | string | yes | Kind is human, agent, bot or controller (docs/actors.md). One of: `human`, `agent`, `bot`, `controller`. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].bundle` | string |  | Bundle, when set, limits the exemption to that version. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].createdBy` | string | yes | CreatedBy is who made the exception. Planned (W6, #2437): admission verifies it is the requester's username. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].environment` | string | yes | Environment is the environment, or the fleet environment, let through. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].expiresAt` | string (date-time) | yes | ExpiresAt ends the exemption. The controller also ends it 24 hours after it first sees it. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].name` | string | yes | Name identifies the exemption (a DNS label), unique in the list. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].namespace` | string | yes | Namespace and Pipeline are the Pipeline let through. |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].pipeline` | string | yes |  |
| `spec.budgetExemptions[].reason` | string | yes | Reason says why (recorded in the BudgetExempted audit record). |
| `spec.budgets` | []object |  | Budgets limit how much the agent promotes before a person looks: versions a day, promotions at once, fleet targets an hour, failures left in place, and a share of a fleet. Every rule that matches a step applies. The four counted limits of all rules sum to at most 1,500, which bounds the ledger in status.usage. Where the controller runs with --agent-budgets, it counts and grants each agent's promotions in status.usage. Not enforced yet: the step hold that makes a step beyond a limit wait rather than fail is W3 (#2434), and the chart's switch, off by default, is W6 (#2437). See docs/design/24-agent-budgets.md. |
| `spec.budgets[].environments` | []string | yes | Environments the rule applies to: exact names, or a prefix ending in "*". A fleet target matches through its own name or its fleet's. |
| `spec.budgets[].fleetShare` | string |  | FleetShare (L5) is the share of one fleet's targets one version of the agent may have under way or failed at once, "1%" to "100%", rounded up and at least one target. It applies to fleet targets only. |
| `spec.budgets[].fleetTargetsPerHour` | integer (int32) |  | FleetTargetsPerHour (L3) is how many fleet targets the agent may start promoting in any hour. Plain environments do not count. |
| `spec.budgets[].maxConcurrent` | integer (int32) |  | MaxConcurrent (L2) is how many of the agent's promotions into these environments may be under way at once. |
| `spec.budgets[].maxUnavailable` | integer (int32) |  | MaxUnavailable (L4) is how many of the agent's promotions may have failed while their environment still runs the failed version. |
| `spec.budgets[].name` | string | yes | Name identifies the rule (a DNS label), unique in the list. |
| `spec.budgets[].namespaces` | []string |  | Namespaces the rule applies to, in the same form. Default: every namespace. Default: `["*"]`. |
| `spec.budgets[].versionsPerDay` | integer (int32) |  | VersionsPerDay (L1) is how many versions the agent may start into these environments in any 24 hours. A version counts once per environment; a fleet's targets are one environment. |
| `spec.description` | string |  | Description says what the agent does. |
| `spec.scope` | object | yes | Scope is where the agent may act. |
| `spec.scope.environments` | []string |  | Environments the agent may approve or override in. Default: all. Default: `["*"]`. |
| `spec.scope.namespaces` | []string |  | Namespaces the agent may write in. Empty: nowhere. |
| `spec.scope.pipelines` | []string |  | Pipelines the agent may create Bundles for. Default: all. Default: `["*"]`. |
| `spec.signingIdentities` | []object |  | SigningIdentities are the Sigstore (Fulcio) certificate identities of the agent's workload. A config commit or an attestation whose verified signer matches exactly one ready, unsuspended AgentIdentity records that agent (commit.agent, attestations.&lt;name&gt;.agent), so a gate can require that the agent that created a version also signed it. See docs/actors.md#signing-identities. |
| `spec.signingIdentities[].issuer` | string | yes | Issuer is the OIDC issuer, for example https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com. |
| `spec.signingIdentities[].subject` | string |  | Subject is the certificate's subject (SAN). |
| `spec.signingIdentities[].subjectRegExp` | string |  | SubjectRegExp is a regular expression the whole subject must match. |
| `spec.sponsor` | object | yes | Sponsor is the person accountable for the agent. |
| `spec.sponsor.team` | string |  | Team is the sponsor's team: shown and exported, not used by policy. |
| `spec.sponsor.user` | string | yes | User is the sponsor's Kubernetes username. |
| `spec.subjects` | []object | yes | Subjects are the principals that are this agent. |
| `spec.subjects[].kind` | string | yes | Kind is ServiceAccount, User (a username exactly as the API server authenticates it, for example an OIDC user) or Group. One of: `ServiceAccount`, `User`, `Group`. |
| `spec.subjects[].name` | string | yes | Name is the ServiceAccount, user or group name. |
| `spec.subjects[].namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the ServiceAccount's namespace. |
| `spec.suspended` | boolean |  | Suspended denies every write by the agent's subjects. An AgentIdentity can be deleted only once it is suspended. |
| `status` | object |  | AgentIdentityStatus is the reconciler's verdict on the registration. |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | Conditions: Ready, with reasons Valid, SubjectConflict, InvalidSponsor and IndexFull. |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status.conditions[].status` | string | yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. One of: `True`, `False`, `Unknown`. |
| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |
| `status.observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | ObservedGeneration is the generation the status describes. |
| `status.ready` | boolean |  | Ready is true when the registration is valid and takes effect. |
| `status.reason` | string |  | Reason says why the AgentIdentity is not ready. |
| `status.usage` | map[string]object |  | Usage is the agent's budget ledgers, one per installation that sees the agent, keyed by the ledger name: --agent-budget-ledger, by default the controller's --agent-index (its release). Each is written by its installation's budget reconciler only (--agent-budgets). An agent without budgets has none. At most 16 ledgers, holding at most 3,000 grants between them (each at most 2,000): the cap keeps one AgentIdentity under etcd's object size limit (docs/design/24-agent-budgets.md section 14). Sixteen is more installations than one agent should span, each counting the agent separately (section 15.2); a 17th installation's status write is refused, so it cannot grant, and its agent steps hold (fail closed) until a ledger is removed. |

## AgentIndex

`kardinal.io/v1alpha1`

AgentIndex is the registry of agents in the shape admission reads: the &lt;release&gt;-actor ValidatingAdmissionPolicy binds it as params. The controller writes its status from the AgentIdentities; one per release, named after the release.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | object |  | AgentIndexStatus maps every registered subject to its agent. |
| `status.bytes` | integer (int64) |  | Bytes is the size of the index's entries as its bound counts them (each entry's JSON, its key and 4 bytes, blocked entries included), also when it is over the bound and written empty. |
| `status.compactGroups` | map[string]string |  | CompactGroups is Groups in the compact format. |
| `status.compactUsers` | map[string]string |  | CompactUsers is Users in the compact format of a later release (#2071): each entry one string. This release never writes it; its CLI and controller read it while Ready's reason is CompactFormat (pkg/actor Readable), so they keep working against a newer release's index. |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | Conditions: Ready (False, reason IndexFull, when the entries are over MaxBytes; False, reason CompactFormat, when a later release wrote the index in the compact format); CompactReady (in the compact format); NearFull (True from 80% of MaxBytes). |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status.conditions[].status` | string | yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. One of: `True`, `False`, `Unknown`. |
| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |
| `status.groups` | map[string]object |  | Groups maps a group to its agent. |
| `status.maxBytes` | integer (int64) |  | MaxBytes is the bound on Bytes: past it the index is not Ready (IndexFull) and the writes the actor policy checks are refused. |
| `status.observedIdentities` | integer |  | ObservedIdentities is how many AgentIdentities the index was built from. |
| `status.users` | map[string]object |  | Users maps a username (ServiceAccount subjects as system:serviceaccount:&lt;namespace&gt;:&lt;name&gt;) to its agent. |

## AgentRun

`kardinal.io/v1alpha1`

AgentRun is one attempt of an in-cluster verifier (a StepTemplate's agent image) for one Bundle, environment and check. Created by the Bundle's kro Graph for a verify gate with verify.run; reconciled by the AgentRun reconciler, which checks its bounds, creates its NetworkPolicy and Job, and records the Job's result.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | AgentRunSpec is one attempt of one in-cluster verifier for one Bundle, environment and check (docs/design/19-verdicts.md, section 8). The kro Graph of the Bundle creates it; the AgentRun reconciler runs the Job whose Pod writes the Verdict. |
| `spec.attempt` | integer | yes | Attempt is the attempt's number (1-based). |
| `spec.bundleName` | string | yes | BundleName is the Bundle verified. |
| `spec.bundleUID` | string | yes | BundleUID is that Bundle's UID. |
| `spec.check` | string | yes | Check is the verify gate's check. |
| `spec.environment` | string | yes | Environment is the environment verified. |
| `spec.pipelineName` | string | yes | PipelineName is the Bundle's Pipeline. |
| `spec.recorded` | string |  | Recorded is set by the Graph: the result of the Verdict named after this AgentRun, when one exists. An AgentRun that starts with it set does not run its Job (an AgentRun deleted and applied again does not run twice). |
| `spec.run` | integer | yes | Run is the run's number among the check's runs (1-based). |
| `spec.targetNamespace` | string | yes | TargetNamespace is the namespace the agent tests: its Pod may reach every Pod there. |
| `spec.template` | string | yes | Template is the StepTemplate the run runs. |
| `spec.version` | string |  | Version is the Bundle's version. |
| `status` | object |  | AgentRunStatus is the observed state of an AgentRun. |
| `status.agent` | string |  | Agent and Sponsor are the agent the run verifies for (its StepTemplate's AgentIdentity) and that agent's sponsor, when the run started. The Graph names them as the actor of the run's Verdict. |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | Conditions: Bounded. |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status.conditions[].status` | string | yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. One of: `True`, `False`, `Unknown`. |
| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |
| `status.deadline` | string (date-time) |  | Deadline is StartedAt plus the template's timeout. |
| `status.finishedAt` | string (date-time) |  | FinishedAt is when the run reached a terminal phase. |
| `status.jobName` | string |  | JobName is the name of the Job the reconciler created. |
| `status.jobUID` | string |  | JobUID is the UID of that Job. A Job of that name with another UID, or none at all, while the run runs fails it: it is not run again. |
| `status.message` | string |  | Message says why the AgentRun is in its phase. |
| `status.phase` | string |  | Phase is Pending until the Job is created, Running while it runs, and Succeeded (the Job completed) or Failed (it failed, timed out, or the run was refused) once it finished, or Skipped. The verify result is the Verdict's, not the phase. One of: `Pending`, `Running`, `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Skipped`. |
| `status.serviceAccount` | string |  | ServiceAccount is the ServiceAccount kardinal created for the run (kr-&lt;run&gt;): the only identity that may write the run's Verdict. It is deleted, with its access, when the run ends. |
| `status.sponsor` | string |  |  |
| `status.startedAt` | string (date-time) |  | StartedAt is when the Job was created. |

## Approval

`kardinal.io/v1alpha1`

Approval records that a person approved, or rejected, a Bundle for an environment. The promotion Graph copies the Approvals of its Bundle into the approval gates of that environment (PolicyGate spec.approvals), and the PolicyGate reconciler counts them against spec.approval.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object | yes | ApprovalSpec is one person's decision on one Bundle in one environment. An Approval is created by kardinal approve and never changed: delete it to revoke the decision. The chart's ValidatingAdmissionPolicy admits it only when spec.user is the requesting user, spec.groups are among the requester's groups, and the kardinal.io/bundle and kardinal.io/environment labels match spec.bundle and spec.environment. |
| `spec.actor` | object |  | Actor is who decided (docs/actors.md): the verified kardinal.io/actor stamp. Its principal equals spec.user. |
| `spec.actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |
| `spec.actor.asserted.client` | string |  | Client is the tool that wrote the record (for example kardinal/0.12.0). |
| `spec.actor.asserted.model` | string |  | Model is the AI model the client says it runs. |
| `spec.actor.asserted.session` | string |  | Session is the client's session or run identifier. |
| `spec.actor.kind` | string | yes | Kind is human, agent, bot or controller (docs/actors.md). One of: `human`, `agent`, `bot`, `controller`. |
| `spec.actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `spec.actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `spec.bundle` | string | yes | Bundle is the name of the Bundle the decision is about, in the Approval's namespace. |
| `spec.bundleUID` | string | yes | BundleUID is the UID of that Bundle: the Graph counts the Approval only for the Bundle with this UID, so an Approval cannot carry over to a new Bundle that reuses the name. |
| `spec.comment` | string |  | Comment is a free-form note shown with the decision. Default: ``. |
| `spec.decision` | string | yes | Decision is approve, or reject: a reject from an allowed approver blocks the gate whatever the other approvals. One of: `approve`, `reject`. Default: `approve`. |
| `spec.environment` | string | yes | Environment is the Pipeline environment the decision is for. |
| `spec.fields` | map[string]string |  | Fields are the structured values the decision carries: the ones the gate's approval.fields declares (a ticket ID, an acknowledgement, a rollback plan URL). An approve that does not satisfy a declared field does not count, and the gate says why (docs/design/23-change-requests.md section 8). They are the approver's statements, verified as theirs, not as true. |
| `spec.groups` | []string |  | Groups are the approver's Kubernetes groups that count for the gate's approval.allowedGroups. Each must be one of the requester's groups. Default: `[]`. |
| `spec.user` | string | yes | User is the Kubernetes username of the approver, as the API server authenticates them (kubectl auth whoami). |

## AuditEvent

`kardinal.io/v1alpha1`

AuditEvent is an immutable record of a single promotion event. It is written once by the PromotionStep reconciler and never updated. AuditEvents form an append-only log of all promotion activity across all pipelines.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | AuditEventSpec defines the immutable record of a single promotion event. AuditEvents are created by the PromotionStep and PolicyGate reconcilers at key lifecycle transitions (started, succeeded, failed). The spec is set at creation; the CRD rejects any later change to it (the rule is on AuditEvent.Spec, so the outbox entries that embed the type, PendingAuditEvent, can be stored in a list). |
| `spec.action` | string | yes | Action is a short verb describing what happened. Valid values: "PromotionStarted", "PromotionSucceeded", "PromotionFailed", "PromotionSuperseded", "PromotionRejected", "RollbackStarted", "RollbackSucceeded", "HealthCheckFailed", "GateBlocked", "GateEvaluated", "GateOverridden", "ApprovalRecorded", "ApprovalRevoked", "HoldCreated", "HoldReleased", "HoldBundleMissing", "BundleRejected", "APIWrite", "VerdictRecorded", "VerdictRevoked", "FreezeExempted", "PipelinePaused", "PipelineResumed", "FreezeStarted", "FreezeLifted", "PRMerged", "ReceiptFailed", "ChangeRequestOpened", "ChangeRequestLinked", "ChangeRequestApproved", "ChangeRequestRejected", "GateChanged". The ChangeRequest actions are written by a per-promotion ChangeRequest when it opens or links its ticket, and when the ticket is first read approved or rejected (docs/design/23-change-requests.md section 9). ReceiptFailed is written by a promotion step that reached Verified without a PromotionReceipt, because its receipt could not be built (status.receiptError). PRMerged is written by a promotion step when its pull request is merged, naming who merged it as the SCM API reports it. ApprovalRecorded and ApprovalRevoked are written by an approval gate when a decision (kardinal approve) appears in or leaves its spec.approvals. BundleRejected is written once when a Bundle's spec.rejected is set (kardinal reject or the UI), naming who rejected it and why; its environment is "*" (the whole Bundle). GateOverridden is written once per spec.overrides entry of a gate instance, naming who created it (kardinal override or the UI). APIWrite is written for each write through the UI API or the Bundle API (controller.accessLog.auditEvents), naming the caller in actor and the route in request. FreezeExempted is written once per exemption when a PromotionStep goes on through an active freeze under it (kardinal override --freeze), naming who made the exemption and why. GateChanged is written by the BundleReconciler when a PolicyGate template that applies to a Promoting version was created, edited or deleted and the version's Graph got the change; gates lists the templates of that rebuild with their old and new digest, one event per version and rebuild (#2144). HealthCheckFailed and GateBlocked are accepted but never written: a failed health check records PromotionFailed (RollbackStarted when onHealthFailure is rollback), and a blocked gate records GateEvaluated with outcome Failure. One of: `PromotionStarted`, `PromotionSucceeded`, `PromotionFailed`, `PromotionSuperseded`, `PromotionRejected`, `RollbackStarted`, `RollbackSucceeded`, `HealthCheckFailed`, `GateBlocked`, `GateEvaluated`, `GateOverridden`, `ApprovalRecorded`, `ApprovalRevoked`, `HoldCreated`, `HoldReleased`, `HoldBundleMissing`, `BundleRejected`, `APIWrite`, `VerdictRecorded`, `VerdictRevoked`, `FreezeExempted`, `PipelinePaused`, `PipelineResumed`, `FreezeStarted`, `FreezeLifted`, `PRMerged`, `ReceiptFailed`, `ChangeRequestOpened`, `ChangeRequestLinked`, `ChangeRequestApproved`, `ChangeRequestRejected`, `GateChanged`. |

A record merged from several gives the net move: an environment in environmentsAdded only ends on, one in environmentsRemoved only ends off, and one in both moved and ended where it started. |

## Bundle

`kardinal.io/v1alpha1`

Bundle is a versioned snapshot of what to deploy. Treat it as immutable: the API does not reject changes to spec, but nothing re-reads a changed one. It carries build provenance and travels through a Pipeline's environments.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | BundleSpec defines the desired state of a Bundle. An image Bundle deploys only its images, so a configRef on it is refused. A Bundle's spec is immutable: spec.type, spec.pipeline, spec.images, spec.chart, spec.configRef, spec.provenance and spec.intent cannot change after creation. The artifact is what gates, verifications and evidence were checked against, and an intent edit would apply only at some later, unrelated re-translation of the Graph; to promote something else, or to another target, create a new Bundle. The rules are transition rules, so they run only on update. |
| `spec.actor` | object |  | Actor is who created the Bundle (docs/actors.md): the verified kardinal.io/actor stamp. kardinal create bundle, the UI and the Bundle API set it; the chart's actor policy admits it only when it says what the requester is. Optional for people and bots, required for agents. |
| `spec.actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |
| `spec.actor.asserted.client` | string |  | Client is the tool that wrote the record (for example kardinal/0.12.0). |
| `spec.actor.asserted.model` | string |  | Model is the AI model the client says it runs. |
| `spec.actor.asserted.session` | string |  | Session is the client's session or run identifier. |
| `spec.actor.kind` | string | yes | Kind is human, agent, bot or controller (docs/actors.md). One of: `human`, `agent`, `bot`, `controller`. |
| `spec.actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `spec.actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `spec.chart` | object |  | Chart is the Helm chart version a "chart" Bundle promotes. The helm-set-image step writes chart.version at update.helm.chartVersionPath. |
| `spec.chart.digest` | string |  | Digest is the chart package digest (index.yaml digest, or the OCI manifest digest). |
| `spec.chart.name` | string | yes | Name is the chart name: letters, digits, ".", "_" and "-", starting and ending with a letter or digit. It is joined into the chart's index and OCI paths, so a "/", "]" or other path character would point the version lookup elsewhere. |
| `spec.chart.repoURL` | string |  | RepoURL is the chart repository (https://... or oci://...). |
| `spec.chart.version` | string | yes | Version is the chart version. |
| `spec.configRef` | object |  | ConfigRef points to the GitOps repository commit this Bundle represents when the bundle type is "config" or "mixed". |
| `spec.configRef.commitSHA` | string |  | CommitSHA is the exact commit SHA for this config snapshot: 4 to 64 hex characters. |
| `spec.configRef.gitRepo` | string |  | GitRepo is the GitOps repository URL. |
| `spec.images` | []object |  | Images lists the container images included in this Bundle, at most 100. |
| `spec.images[].digest` | string |  | Digest is the image digest (sha256:...), in the OCI digest grammar. |
| `spec.images[].repository` | string | yes | Repository is the image repository (e.g. "ghcr.io/nginx/nginx"). |
| `spec.images[].tag` | string |  | Tag is the image tag, in the OCI distribution grammar: up to 128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_.-], not starting with "." or "-". |
| `spec.intent` | object |  | Intent declares optional targeting and skip overrides for this Bundle. |
| `spec.intent.skipEnvironments` | []string |  | SkipEnvironments lists environment names to exclude from this promotion, subject to the PolicyGate SkipPermission check. |
| `spec.intent.targetEnvironment` | string |  | TargetEnvironment restricts this Bundle to promoting only up to and including this environment. Empty means promote through all environments. |
| `spec.intent.targetOnly` | boolean |  | TargetOnly promotes only TargetEnvironment (for a fleet, its targets) when every environment upstream of it has verified this Bundle's artifacts, pinned by digest, in another Bundle of the Pipeline: the BundleReconciler records that verification in status.upstreamEvidence when it first builds the Graph, and the Graph has no upstream environment. When one has not, the Bundle promotes through them, as without TargetOnly, and its UpstreamEvidence condition says why. kardinal rollback, kardinal promote and the automatic rollback set it (#1311). |
| `spec.pipeline` | string | yes | Pipeline is the name of the Pipeline this Bundle targets. |
| `spec.provenance` | object |  | Provenance carries build metadata for audit and rollback. |
| `spec.provenance.author` | string |  | Author is the committer or triggering actor for this build. |
| `spec.provenance.ciRunURL` | string |  | CIRunURL is the URL of the CI run that built this Bundle. It must not carry credentials: no user info, no credential query or fragment parameter (a name ending in token, secret, key, signature, password, session, ticket, bearer, ..., except harmless ones such as monkey; or sig, auth, authorization, jwt, code, sid; any case, with or without -, _ or an array index), and no percent-encoded parameter name. The PR body publishes it, and a promotion receipt signs it (its Rekor sink publishes it for good). The rules are pkg/urlsecret's (CRDRules). |
| `spec.provenance.commitSHA` | string |  | CommitSHA is the application source commit that produced this Bundle: 4 to 64 hex characters. An image Subscription records the commit the image's build recorded in org.opencontainers.image.revision (a full SHA), and none when the image names none. Versions a Subscription created before v0.12.0 may hold the image digest instead, which the pattern still accepts so they stay valid. |
| `spec.provenance.commitTime` | string (date-time) |  | CommitTime is when the source commit (CommitSHA) was made, for CI to set (`kardinal create bundle --commit-time`). The lead time metrics (status.metrics.commitToProductionMinutes, the Pipeline's deploymentMetrics) start at it; without it they start at the Bundle's creation, which leaves out the build. The Bundle API and the CLI refuse a zero time, one more than 5 minutes in the future and one more than a year old; a time after the Bundle's creation or more than a year before it is ignored. |
| `spec.provenance.rollbackFrom` | string |  | RollbackFrom is, on a rollback Bundle, the Bundle it rolls back from: the one deployed in the environment when it was planned, which the kardinal.io/rollback-from annotation also names. spec.provenance is immutable, so unlike the annotation it cannot be relinked later: the controller binds an automatic rollback to the failing Bundle on it (#2225). Rollbacks created before v0.13.0 do not have it. |
| `spec.provenance.rollbackOf` | string |  | RollbackOf is the name of the Bundle this Bundle rolls back (if any). |
| `spec.provenance.timestamp` | string (date-time) |  | Timestamp is when the bundle was built. |
| `spec.rejected` | object |  | Rejected marks the Bundle as rejected (kardinal reject): it is never promoted again, its in-flight steps are cancelled, and rollback, promote and Subscriptions skip any Bundle carrying its artifacts. Setting it is one-way: it cannot be changed or removed. The chart's ValidatingAdmissionPolicy requires rejected.by to be the requesting user; without that policy nothing checks it. |
| `spec.rejected.actor` | object |  | Actor is By's actor stamp (docs/actors.md), checked by the chart's actor admission policy; the BundleRejected AuditEvent names it. |
| `spec.rejected.actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.rejected.actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |
| `spec.rejected.actor.asserted.client` | string |  | Client is the tool that wrote the record (for example kardinal/0.12.0). |
| `spec.rejected.actor.asserted.model` | string |  | Model is the AI model the client says it runs. |
| `spec.rejected.actor.asserted.session` | string |  | Session is the client's session or run identifier. |
| `spec.rejected.actor.kind` | string | yes | Kind is human, agent, bot or controller (docs/actors.md). One of: `human`, `agent`, `bot`, `controller`. |
| `spec.rejected.actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `spec.rejected.actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.rejected.actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `spec.rejected.at` | string (date-time) |  | At is when the Bundle was rejected. |
| `spec.rejected.by` | string | yes | By is the Kubernetes username of whoever rejected the Bundle. The chart's ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (kardinal-identity) admits a new rejection only when by equals the requesting user's username. |
| `spec.rejected.reason` | string | yes | Reason says why the Bundle was rejected. |
| `spec.type` | string | yes | Type classifies the bundle content. Supersession rule: each bundle type supersedes only bundles of the same type. An image bundle does NOT supersede a config bundle and vice versa. This allows image and config promotions to coexist independently in the same pipeline. A chart Bundle promotes a Helm chart version (spec.chart) with update.strategy helm. One of: `image`, `config`, `mixed`, `chart`. |
| `status` | object |  | BundleStatus defines the observed state of a Bundle. |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | Conditions holds status conditions. |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status.conditions[].status` | string | yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. One of: `True`, `False`, `Unknown`. |
| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |
| `status.environments` | []object |  | Environments holds per-environment promotion evidence. |
| `status.environments[].healthCheckedAt` | string (date-time) |  | HealthCheckedAt is when the post-merge health check completed. |
| `status.environments[].name` | string | yes | Name is the environment name. |
| `status.environments[].phase` | string |  | Phase is the promotion phase for this environment. |
| `status.environments[].prURL` | string |  | PRURL is the URL of the pull request opened for this promotion. |
| `status.environments[].soakMinutes` | integer (int64) |  | SoakMinutes is the number of minutes that have elapsed since HealthCheckedAt. Written by the BundleReconciler as part of its own CRD status write. The PolicyGate reconciler reads this field from Bundle.status.environments to populate bundle.upstreamSoakMinutes in the CEL context, so the gate does not read the clock. |
| `status.graphRef` | string |  | GraphRef is the name of the kro Graph CR backing this Bundle's promotion DAG. Populated by the BundleReconciler when the Graph is first created. Used to detect Graph deletion and trigger recreation. The Graph of a Bundle that failed promoting is not recreated (GraphSynced=False, reason GraphDeleted), so the failed artifacts are not promoted again; a Pipeline change rebuilds it. |
| `status.metrics` | object |  | Metrics holds deployment efficiency metrics for this Bundle. Populated by the BundleReconciler when all environments reach Verified. |
| `status.metrics.bakeResets` | integer |  | BakeResets is the total number of bake timer resets across all environments. High bake reset count indicates flaky health or over-sensitive bake windows. |
| `status.metrics.commitToProductionMinutes` | integer (int64) |  | CommitToProductionMinutes is the time from the commit (spec.provenance.commitTime, else the Bundle's creation) to the last environment's health check passing. |
| `status.metrics.operatorInterventions` | integer |  | OperatorInterventions is the number of PolicyGate overrides recorded on this Bundle's gate instances (kardinal override), counted when the Bundle becomes Verified. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents` | []object |  | PendingAuditEvents are the BundleRejected AuditEvents the Bundle reconciler has recorded but not written yet (the audit outbox, #1552): the entry is stored in the same status write that sets phase Rejected, and removed once its AuditEvent exists. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].createdAt` | string |  | CreatedAt is the transition time in RFC 3339 with nanoseconds, written to the AuditEvent's kardinal.io/created-at annotation: spec.timestamp has one-second resolution. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].labels` | map[string]string |  | Labels are the AuditEvent's labels. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].name` | string | yes | Name is the AuditEvent's name. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec` | object | yes | Spec is the AuditEvent's spec, timestamp included: the record carries the time of the transition, not the time it was written. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.action` | string | yes | Action is a short verb describing what happened. Valid values: "PromotionStarted", "PromotionSucceeded", "PromotionFailed", "PromotionSuperseded", "PromotionRejected", "RollbackStarted", "RollbackSucceeded", "HealthCheckFailed", "GateBlocked", "GateEvaluated", "GateOverridden", "ApprovalRecorded", "ApprovalRevoked", "HoldCreated", "HoldReleased", "HoldBundleMissing", "BundleRejected", "APIWrite", "VerdictRecorded", "VerdictRevoked", "FreezeExempted", "PipelinePaused", "PipelineResumed", "FreezeStarted", "FreezeLifted", "PRMerged", "ReceiptFailed", "ChangeRequestOpened", "ChangeRequestLinked", "ChangeRequestApproved", "ChangeRequestRejected", "GateChanged". The ChangeRequest actions are written by a per-promotion ChangeRequest when it opens or links its ticket, and when the ticket is first read approved or rejected (docs/design/23-change-requests.md section 9). ReceiptFailed is written by a promotion step that reached Verified without a PromotionReceipt, because its receipt could not be built (status.receiptError). PRMerged is written by a promotion step when its pull request is merged, naming who merged it as the SCM API reports it. ApprovalRecorded and ApprovalRevoked are written by an approval gate when a decision (kardinal approve) appears in or leaves its spec.approvals. BundleRejected is written once when a Bundle's spec.rejected is set (kardinal reject or the UI), naming who rejected it and why; its environment is "*" (the whole Bundle). GateOverridden is written once per spec.overrides entry of a gate instance, naming who created it (kardinal override or the UI). APIWrite is written for each write through the UI API or the Bundle API (controller.accessLog.auditEvents), naming the caller in actor and the route in request. GateChanged is written by the BundleReconciler when a PolicyGate template that applies to a Promoting version was created, edited or deleted and the version's Graph got the change; gates lists the templates of that rebuild with their old and new digest, one event per version and rebuild (#2144). HealthCheckFailed and GateBlocked are accepted but never written: a failed health check records PromotionFailed (RollbackStarted when onHealthFailure is rollback), and a blocked gate records GateEvaluated with outcome Failure. | `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.timestamp` | string (date-time) | yes | Timestamp is when the event occurred (RFC 3339 format). |
| `status.phase` | string |  | Phase is the bundle promotion phase. Rejected is final: spec.rejected is set, and nothing of this Bundle is promoted again. One of: `Available`, `Promoting`, `Verified`, `Failed`, `Superseded`, `Rejected`. |
| `status.phaseTransitionTime` | string (date-time) |  | PhaseTransitionTime is when phase last changed: when the version became Promoting, Verified, Failed, Superseded or Rejected. The NotificationHook events of a phase change carry it as their time. |
| `status.pipelineSpecHash` | string |  | PipelineSpecHash is the SHA-256 hash of the Pipeline spec (spec.paused excluded) the Graph was last built from. When the Bundle reconciler is re-queued by a Pipeline watch event, it compares the current Pipeline spec hash to this field. A mismatch re-translates the Graph in place with the updated spec. |
| `status.policyGatesHash` | string |  | PolicyGatesHash is the SHA-256 hash of the PolicyGate templates that apply to the Pipeline's environments, recorded when the Graph is built and when it could not be built (InvalidSpec, reason GraphBuildFailed). A change to those templates re-translates the Graph of a Promoting Bundle in place, and retries one that could not be built, as a Pipeline change does. |
| `status.rejectedArtifacts` | object |  | RejectedArtifacts is what a rejection (spec.rejected) rejects: the artifacts of this Bundle that differ from what was Verified before it in the environments it reached, written by the Bundle reconciler when it marks the Bundle Rejected. A sidecar the Bundle carries unchanged is not in it, so rolling back to the Bundle before stays possible. Unset (a rejection not processed yet) means all of the Bundle's artifacts. |
| `status.rejectedArtifacts.comparedWith` | []string |  | ComparedWith names, per environment, the Verified Bundle the artifacts were compared with ("&lt;env&gt;=&lt;bundle&gt;"); empty when no environment had one, and then every artifact is rejected. |
| `status.rejectedArtifacts.configCommitSHA` | string |  | ConfigCommitSHA is the rejected config commit, when it differs. |
| `status.rejectedArtifacts.images` | []object |  | Images are the rejected images: those not Verified, with the same digest (or tag, without a digest), before this Bundle in every environment it reached. |
| `status.rejectedArtifacts.images[].digest` | string |  | Digest is the image digest (sha256:...), in the OCI digest grammar. |
| `status.rejectedArtifacts.images[].repository` | string | yes | Repository is the image repository (e.g. "ghcr.io/nginx/nginx"). |
| `status.rejectedArtifacts.images[].tag` | string |  | Tag is the image tag, in the OCI distribution grammar: up to 128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_.-], not starting with "." or "-". |
| `status.retiredAt` | string (date-time) |  | RetiredAt is when the Bundle's Graph was retired: set in the same write as RetiredSteps, and never cleared. A Bundle with RetiredAt is final; the GraphRetired condition only shows the retirement's progress. |
| `status.retiredSteps` | []object |  | RetiredSteps records the PromotionSteps of a Bundle whose Graph was retired (condition GraphRetired=True). Deleting a finished Bundle's Graph deletes the PromotionSteps, PolicyGate instances and PRStatuses it created, so kro does not hold every finished Graph in memory. Rollback, promote, history, metrics, the CLI and the UI read these records where they read the steps of a Bundle that is still promoting. The step of a fleet target removed from the Pipeline while the Bundle promoted is recorded here when its Graph is updated, before kro prunes it, and kept at the retirement. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes | CreatedAt is the PromotionStep's creationTimestamp. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].deployedAt` | string (date-time) |  | DeployedAt is when the step's change reached its environment: the start of its health-check step. The deployment metrics count a retired Bundle from it. Records written before this field have none. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].environment` | string | yes | Environment is the PromotionStep's spec.environment. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].healthCheckExpiry` | string (date-time) |  | HealthCheckExpiry is the PromotionStep's status.healthCheckExpiry: set once its change merged and the health check started. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].markerDigest` | string |  | MarkerDigest is the marker digest of the step's render (layout: branch): status.outputs.markerDigest. Later renders of the environment accept it as kardinal's after the RenderRun that wrote it was deleted with the Graph. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].message` | string |  | Message is the PromotionStep's final status.message, cut to 512 bytes. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].name` | string | yes | Name is the PromotionStep's name. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].noChanges` | boolean |  | NoChanges is the step's status.outputs.noChanges: the environment already had the change, so the step deployed nothing. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].prURL` | string |  | PRURL is the PromotionStep's status.prURL. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].renderRequested` | boolean |  | RenderRequested is true when the step asked for its render (layout: branch): a Failed step that did may have lost a render that pushed. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].state` | string |  | State is the PromotionStep's final status.state. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].stepType` | string |  | StepType is the PromotionStep's spec.stepType. |
| `status.retiredSteps[].verifiedAt` | string (date-time) |  | VerifiedAt is when the PromotionStep became Verified. |
| `status.upstreamEvidence` | []object |  | UpstreamEvidence is, for a Bundle with spec.intent.targetOnly, the verification of its artifacts in each environment upstream of its target by another Bundle of the Pipeline. This Bundle does not promote those environments, so they are not in environments; gates read their soak from here. Recorded once, when the Graph is first built; empty when the Bundle promotes through them. |
| `status.upstreamEvidence[].bundle` | string | yes | Bundle is the Bundle of the same Pipeline, with the same artifacts, whose promotion was Verified in Environment. |
| `status.upstreamEvidence[].environment` | string | yes | Environment is the upstream environment. |
| `status.upstreamEvidence[].replacedAt` | string (date-time) |  | ReplacedAt is when another version (other artifacts) first started promoting to Environment after VerifiedAt: from then on Bundle's artifacts no longer ran there. Unset while they still do. |
| `status.upstreamEvidence[].soakMinutes` | integer (int64) |  | SoakMinutes is the number of minutes from VerifiedAt to ReplacedAt, or to now while it is unset: how long the artifacts ran there. Written by the BundleReconciler like EnvironmentStatus.SoakMinutes. |
| `status.upstreamEvidence[].verifiedAt` | string (date-time) | yes | VerifiedAt is when that promotion's health check completed (its status.environments healthCheckedAt). |
| `status.version` | string |  | Version is what the Bundle ships, for display: the image tag (the images, when several), "config &lt;sha&gt;", or the chart name and version. Written by the BundleReconciler from spec. |

## ChangeRequest

`kardinal.io/v1alpha1`

ChangeRequest is a change request a promotion waits for (docs/design/23-change-requests.md).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | ChangeRequestSpec defines a change request: a ticket in a ticketing system (ServiceNow, Jira) that kardinal opens, or links, for a promotion into an environment, and whose state a PolicyGate waits for (changeRequests.&lt;name&gt; in its expression). A template (perPromotion: true) is not itself a ticket: the promotion Graph creates one instance per Bundle and environment whose gates read changeRequests.&lt;name&gt;, once the environment's upstreams are Verified. Only the ChangeRequest reconciler calls the provider, and only it writes status. |
| `spec.appliesTo` | []string |  | AppliesTo, when set, limits the environments that get an instance to these (a fleet target counts as its fleet). Unset: every environment whose gates read changeRequests.&lt;name&gt;. |
| `spec.jira` | object |  | Jira configures provider jira. |
| `spec.jira.apiVersion` | string |  | APIVersion is the REST API version: 3 for Jira Cloud (a description is sent as an Atlassian Document Format paragraph), 2 for Jira Data Center. One of: `2`, `3`. Default: `3`. |
| `spec.jira.approvedResolutions` | []string |  | ApprovedResolutions are the resolution names that count as approved: with ApprovedStatuses unset, an issue in ApprovedStatusCategory is approved only with one of them (many workflows move an issue to a done status such as Declined without a resolution); with ApprovedStatuses set, an issue in one of them is approved unresolved or with one of them. Any other resolution (Duplicate, Declined, one nobody configured) is closed, never approved. |
| `spec.jira.approvedStatusCategory` | string |  | ApprovedStatusCategory is the status category (new, indeterminate, done) that, with ApprovedStatuses unset, approves an issue resolved in ApprovedResolutions (an unresolved one never). One of: `new`, `indeterminate`, `done`. Default: `done`. |
| `spec.jira.approvedStatuses` | []string |  | ApprovedStatuses are the status names that mean approved; when unset, a status in ApprovedStatusCategory does. |
| `spec.jira.baseURL` | string | yes | BaseURL is the Jira site, https://&lt;site&gt;.atlassian.net or a Data Center base URL. |
| `spec.jira.cancelledResolutions` | []string |  | CancelledResolutions are the resolution names that mean cancelled (default: Won't Do). |
| `spec.jira.credentialsSecretRef` | object | yes | CredentialsSecretRef names the Secret key that holds the credential: a token, or "user:password" for basic. The Secret must be in the ChangeRequest's namespace and labelled kardinal.io/referenceable=true. |
| `spec.jira.credentialsSecretRef.key` | string | yes | Key is the key in the Secret's data. |
| `spec.jira.credentialsSecretRef.name` | string | yes | Name is the Secret name. |
| `spec.jira.issueType` | string |  | IssueType is the issue type opened (Change, Task, ...). Default: `Task`. |
| `spec.jira.linkProjects` | []string |  | LinkProjects are further project keys a linked issue may be in. |
| `spec.jira.project` | string | yes | Project is the key of the project issues are opened in, searched and linked from (with LinkProjects). An issue of any other project is refused. |
| `spec.jira.rejectedStatuses` | []string |  | RejectedStatuses are the status names that mean rejected. |
| `spec.jira.scheme` | string |  | Scheme is basic (the key holds user:password, or Jira Cloud's email:api-token) or bearer (an OAuth token, or a Jira Data Center PAT). One of: `basic`, `bearer`. Default: `basic`. |
| `spec.jira.template` | map[string]string |  | Template are the fields the issue is created with (summary, description), with the same placeholders as ServiceNow's. |
| `spec.link` | object |  | Link says where mode link reads the ticket key. |
| `spec.link.from` | string | yes | From is approvalField (a structured approval field of the environment's counted approvals), bundleLabel or bundleAnnotation. One of: `approvalField`, `bundleLabel`, `bundleAnnotation`. |
| `spec.link.name` | string | yes | Name is the approval field, label or annotation. |
| `spec.link.requireField` | object |  | RequireField, when set, verifies a linked ticket that does not carry the promotion's correlation id: its field Name must equal Value (for example cmdb_ci), it must have been created after the Bundle, and no other ChangeRequest may hold it since earlier. Without it, a ticket is verified only when it carries the correlation id; otherwise status.verified is false. |
| `spec.link.requireField.name` | string | yes |  |
| `spec.link.requireField.value` | string | yes |  |
| `spec.mode` | string |  | Mode is open (kardinal creates the ticket) or link (kardinal reads its key from spec.link and tracks it, never creating one). One of: `open`, `link`. Default: `open`. |
| `spec.perPromotion` | boolean |  | PerPromotion makes this ChangeRequest a template: the Graph creates an instance of it per Bundle and environment whose gates read changeRequests.&lt;name&gt;. A ChangeRequest without it is not used by a promotion. |
| `spec.pollInterval` | string |  | PollInterval is how often the ticket's state is read: at least 30s, default 1m. A webhook trigger (POST /webhook/changerequests/...) reads it at once. Default: `1m`. |
| `spec.provider` | string | yes | Provider is the ticketing system. One of: `servicenow`, `jira`. |
| `spec.servicenow` | object |  | ServiceNow configures provider servicenow. |
| `spec.servicenow.credentialsSecretRef` | object | yes | CredentialsSecretRef names the Secret key that holds the credential: a token, or "user:password" for basic. The Secret must be in the ChangeRequest's namespace and labelled kardinal.io/referenceable=true. |
| `spec.servicenow.credentialsSecretRef.key` | string | yes | Key is the key in the Secret's data. |
| `spec.servicenow.credentialsSecretRef.name` | string | yes | Name is the Secret name. |
| `spec.servicenow.instanceURL` | string | yes | InstanceURL is the ServiceNow instance, https://&lt;instance&gt;.service-now.com. |
| `spec.servicenow.integrationUser` | string |  | IntegrationUser is the ServiceNow user_name the credential acts as. kardinal adopts an existing change (a create whose answer it lost) only when that user created it (sys_created_by), so nobody can plant a labelled change and approve it. With scheme basic it defaults to the credential's user; scheme bearer needs it. |
| `spec.servicenow.scheme` | string |  | Scheme is basic (the key holds user:password, or Jira Cloud's email:api-token) or bearer (an OAuth token, or a Jira Data Center PAT). One of: `basic`, `bearer`. Default: `basic`. |
| `spec.servicenow.states` | map[string]string |  | States maps state values of the change_request state field (the raw value, -2, or its display name, Scheduled) to kardinal states, before the default Change Management state model (docs/change-requests.md). |
| `spec.servicenow.template` | map[string]string |  | Template are the fields the change request is created with (short_description, assignment_group, ...): string values, with the placeholders of a per-promotion MetricCheck ({{ bundle.version }}, {{ pipeline.name }}, {{ environment.name }}, ...). |
| `spec.servicenow.type` | string |  | Type is the change model of the Change Management API: normal, standard or emergency. One of: `normal`, `standard`, `emergency`. Default: `normal`. |
| `spec.suspend` | boolean |  | Suspend stops reading the ticket (the Graph sets it on an instance once its Bundle stops promoting). The last state stays in status and goes stale. |
| `spec.timeout` | string |  | Timeout is how long after the instance's first read status.timedOut becomes true; the gate's expression decides what that means. Default 24h; "0" for none. Default: `24h`. |
| `spec.webhook` | object |  | Webhook, on a template, lets the ticketing system trigger a read of its instances' tickets at once: POST /webhook/changerequests/&lt;namespace&gt;/&lt;name&gt; with the token in the X-Kardinal-Token header (or as a last path segment). The request only sets the instances' kardinal.io/refresh annotation; its body is never read for state. Polling stays correct without it. |
| `spec.webhook.secretRef` | object | yes | SecretRef names a Secret in the ChangeRequest's namespace, labelled kardinal.io/referenceable=true, whose key "token" (at least 16 characters) authenticates a trigger: the X-Kardinal-Token header, or the last path segment of the webhook URL. |
| `spec.webhook.secretRef.name` | string | yes | Name is the Secret name. |
| `status` | object |  | ChangeRequestStatus is written by the ChangeRequest reconciler only. |
| `status.approvers` | []object |  | Approvers are the ticket's approvers, when the provider exposes them. |
| `status.approvers[].at` | string (date-time) |  |  |
| `status.approvers[].decision` | string |  | Decision is the provider's (approved, rejected, requested). |
| `status.approvers[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | Conditions: Ready, Stale, CredentialsInvalid, Refused (egress) and ProviderError. |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status.conditions[].status` | string | yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. One of: `True`, `False`, `Unknown`. |
| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |
| `status.correlationID` | string |  | CorrelationID is the promotion's id written into the ticket (kardinal:&lt;namespace&gt;/&lt;bundle&gt;/&lt;environment&gt;/&lt;bundle UID&gt;). |
| `status.linkedAt` | string (date-time) |  | LinkedAt is when this instance linked its ticket key; of two ChangeRequests that link one ticket, the earlier keeps it. |
| `status.observedAt` | string (date-time) |  | ObservedAt is the last successful read of the ticket. |
| `status.observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | ObservedGeneration is the generation of the spec last acted on. |
| `status.observedRefresh` | string |  | ObservedRefresh is the kardinal.io/refresh annotation (a webhook trigger) the reconciler last answered with a read. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents` | []object |  | PendingAuditEvents are ChangeRequestOpened, ChangeRequestLinked, ChangeRequestApproved and ChangeRequestRejected records not yet written (the audit outbox). |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].createdAt` | string |  | CreatedAt is the transition time in RFC 3339 with nanoseconds, written to the AuditEvent's kardinal.io/created-at annotation: spec.timestamp has one-second resolution. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].labels` | map[string]string |  | Labels are the AuditEvent's labels. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].name` | string | yes | Name is the AuditEvent's name. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec` | object | yes | Spec is the AuditEvent's spec, timestamp included: the record carries the time of the transition, not the time it was written. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.action` | string | yes | Action is a short verb describing what happened. Valid values: "PromotionStarted", "PromotionSucceeded", "PromotionFailed", "PromotionSuperseded", "PromotionRejected", "RollbackStarted", "RollbackSucceeded", "HealthCheckFailed", "GateBlocked", "GateEvaluated", "GateOverridden", "ApprovalRecorded", "ApprovalRevoked", "HoldCreated", "HoldReleased", "HoldBundleMissing", "BundleRejected", "APIWrite", "VerdictRecorded", "VerdictRevoked", "FreezeExempted", "PipelinePaused", "PipelineResumed", "FreezeStarted", "FreezeLifted", "PRMerged", "ReceiptFailed", "ChangeRequestOpened", "ChangeRequestLinked", "ChangeRequestApproved", "ChangeRequestRejected", "GateChanged". The ChangeRequest actions are written by a per-promotion ChangeRequest when it opens or links its ticket, and when the ticket is first read approved or rejected (docs/design/23-change-requests.md section 9). ReceiptFailed is written by a promotion step that reached Verified without a PromotionReceipt, because its receipt could not be built (status.receiptError). PRMerged is written by a promotion step when its pull request is merged, naming who merged it as the SCM API reports it. ApprovalRecorded and ApprovalRevoked are written by an approval gate when a decision (kardinal approve) appears in or leaves its spec.approvals. BundleRejected is written once when a Bundle's spec.rejected is set (kardinal reject or the UI), naming who rejected it and why; its environment is "*" (the whole Bundle). GateOverridden is written once per spec.overrides entry of a gate instance, naming who created it (kardinal override or the UI). APIWrite is written for each write through the UI API or the Bundle API (controller.accessLog.auditEvents), naming the caller in actor and the route in request. FreezeExempted is written once per exemption when a PromotionStep goes on through an active freeze under it (kardinal override --freeze), naming who made the exemption and why. GateChanged is written by the BundleReconciler when a PolicyGate template that applies to a Promoting version was created, edited or deleted and the version's Graph got the change; gates lists the templates of that rebuild with their old and new digest, one event per version and rebuild (#2144). HealthCheckFailed and GateBlocked are accepted but never written: a failed health check records PromotionFailed (RollbackStarted when onHealthFailure is rollback), and a blocked gate records GateEvaluated with outcome Failure. One of: `PromotionStarted`, `PromotionSucceeded`, `PromotionFailed`, `PromotionSuperseded`, `PromotionRejected`, `RollbackStarted`, `RollbackSucceeded`, `HealthCheckFailed`, `GateBlocked`, `GateEvaluated`, `GateOverridden`, `ApprovalRecorded`, `ApprovalRevoked`, `HoldCreated`, `HoldReleased`, `HoldBundleMissing`, `BundleRejected`, `APIWrite`, `VerdictRecorded`, `VerdictRevoked`, `FreezeExempted`, `PipelinePaused`, `PipelineResumed`, `FreezeStarted`, `FreezeLifted`, `PRMerged`, `ReceiptFailed`, `ChangeRequestOpened`, `ChangeRequestLinked`, `ChangeRequestApproved`, `ChangeRequestRejected`, `GateChanged`. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor` | object |  | Actor is who caused the event (docs/actors.md). Absent on records written before v0.12. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.asserted.client` | string |  | Client is the tool that wrote the record (for example kardinal/0.12.0). |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.asserted.model` | string |  | Model is the AI model the client says it runs. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.asserted.session` | string |  | Session is the client's session or run identifier. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.kind` | string | yes | Kind is human, agent, bot or controller (docs/actors.md). One of: `human`, `agent`, `bot`, `controller`. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.bundleName` | string |  | BundleName is the name of the Bundle being promoted. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.environment` | string |  | Environment is the environment name where the event occurred. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.fields` | map[string]string |  | Fields are an ApprovalRecorded or ApprovalRevoked decision's structured values (Approval spec.fields) the gate declares, whole. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates` | []object |  | Gates are the PolicyGate template changes a GateChanged event records: one event per version and rebuild, listing at most MaxAuditGateChanges changes in template order. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].environmentsAdded` | []string |  | EnvironmentsAdded are environments of the version the template's gate copies now apply to and did not before (a kardinal.io/applies-to edit moves a gate without changing its rule): the first 5 in name order. A record merged from several gives the net move: an environment in environmentsAdded only ends on, one in environmentsRemoved only ends off, and one in both moved and ended where it started. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].environmentsOmitted` | integer (int32) |  | EnvironmentsOmitted is one count, for environmentsAdded and environmentsRemoved together, of the environments past the first 5 of each. In a record merged from several it is an upper bound. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].environmentsRemoved` | []string |  | EnvironmentsRemoved are environments of the version the template's gate copies applied to and no longer do: the first 5 in name order. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].manager` | string |  | Manager is the field manager of the template's newest managedFields entry, as the writing client declared it (kubectl --field-manager sets any name). It is not verified and does not say who wrote the template: the API server's audit log does. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].namespace` | string | yes | Namespace is the template's namespace. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].newDigest` | string |  | NewDigest is the digest the instances have now. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].newGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | NewGeneration is the template generation the instances have now. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].oldDigest` | string |  | OldDigest is the digest the instances had. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].oldGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | OldGeneration is the template generation the instances had. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].template` | string | yes | Template is the PolicyGate template's name. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gatesOmitted` | integer (int32) |  | GatesOmitted counts the changes of the same rebuild that Gates leaves out, past its first MaxAuditGateChanges. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.mergedRecords` | integer (int32) |  | MergedRecords is how many unwritten records this one replaces: a full audit outbox merges records of the same kind (GateChanged) before it drops any, during an AuditEvent write outage. Absent for a record written as it was recorded. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.message` | string |  | Message is a human-readable description of the event. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.outcome` | string | yes | Outcome describes the result of the action. Valid values: "Success", "Failure", "Pending". One of: `Success`, `Failure`, `Pending`. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.pipelineName` | string |  | PipelineName is the name of the Pipeline the Bundle is promoting through. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.request` | object |  | Request is the API request of an APIWrite event. It records no body and no token. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.request.method` | string | yes | Method is the HTTP method. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.request.route` | string | yes | Route is the API route pattern, for example /api/v1/ui/pipelines/{name}/pause. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.timestamp` | string (date-time) | yes | Timestamp is when the event occurred (RFC 3339 format). |
| `status.pendingCreate` | object |  | PendingCreate is a create in flight (the outbox, see ChangeRequestPendingCreate). |
| `status.pendingCreate.correlationID` | string | yes | CorrelationID is the id the create carries. |
| `status.pendingCreate.since` | string (date-time) | yes | Since is when the create was first attempted. |
| `status.providerState` | string |  | ProviderState is the raw state, for people. |
| `status.ready` | boolean |  | Ready is true once the reconciler has a ticket and has read its state. |
| `status.retryAt` | string (date-time) |  | RetryAt, after a provider error or a 429, is when the next request is sent. |
| `status.startedAt` | string (date-time) |  | StartedAt is the instance's first reconcile: the timeout counts from it. |
| `status.state` | string |  | State is the normalised state: pending, approved, rejected, cancelled, closed or unknown. One of: `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `closed`, `unknown`. |
| `status.ticket` | object |  | Ticket is the ticket the instance tracks. |
| `status.ticket.id` | string |  | ID is the ServiceNow sys_id or the Jira issue id. |
| `status.ticket.key` | string | yes | Key is the ServiceNow number (CHG0031337) or the Jira issue key (CHG-42). |
| `status.ticket.url` | string |  | URL is the ticket's page. |
| `status.timedOut` | boolean |  | TimedOut is true once spec.timeout has passed since StartedAt. |
| `status.validUntil` | string (date-time) |  | ValidUntil is ObservedAt plus twice pollInterval: a gate evaluated after it reads changeRequests.&lt;name&gt;.stale as true. |
| `status.verified` | boolean |  | Verified, for a linked ticket, reports whether it is this promotion's: it carries the correlation id, or it satisfies link.requireField, was created after the Bundle, and no other ChangeRequest holds it since earlier. An unverified link is tracked but says so (VerifiedReason). |
| `status.verifiedReason` | string |  | VerifiedReason says why a linked ticket is, or is not, verified. |

## ChangeWindow

`kardinal.io/v1alpha1`

ChangeWindow defines a cluster-scoped time window during which promotions are blocked. Without spec.freeze, a ChangeWindow blocks nothing by itself: a PolicyGate blocks while a window it references is active, for example !changewindow.isBlocked("holiday-freeze") or changewindow.isAllowed("business-hours"). A gate that names a ChangeWindow that does not exist blocks. With spec.freeze, the window holds the promotions it selects while it is active.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | ChangeWindowSpec defines the desired state of a ChangeWindow. |
| `spec.end` | string (date-time) |  | End is when a blackout window ends (required for type: blackout, except with spec.freeze: a freeze without end lasts until it is removed). |
| `spec.freeze` | object |  | Freeze makes the window hold promotions by itself while it is active, without a gate naming it (docs/design/18-actor-policy.md): an agent freeze, or a stop-the-line for everyone. kardinal freeze writes it. |
| `spec.freeze.actor` | object |  | Actor is CreatedBy's actor stamp (docs/actors.md), checked by the chart's actor admission policy; the FreezeStarted AuditEvent names it. |
| `spec.freeze.actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.freeze.actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |
| `spec.freeze.actor.asserted.client` | string |  | Client is the tool that wrote the record (for example kardinal/0.12.0). |
| `spec.freeze.actor.asserted.model` | string |  | Model is the AI model the client says it runs. |
| `spec.freeze.actor.asserted.session` | string |  | Session is the client's session or run identifier. |
| `spec.freeze.actor.kind` | string | yes | Kind is human, agent, bot or controller (docs/actors.md). One of: `human`, `agent`, `bot`, `controller`. |
| `spec.freeze.actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `spec.freeze.actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.freeze.actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `spec.freeze.actors` | string | yes | Actors is whose versions are held: agents (versions whose actor stamp says kind agent) or everyone (stop-the-line). One of: `agents`, `everyone`. |
| `spec.freeze.createdBy` | string |  | CreatedBy is who froze: the chart's freezes admission policy admits it only as the requester's username, and it never changes. |
| `spec.freeze.exemptionRecords` | []object |  | ExemptionRecords has one record per spec.freeze.exemptions entry: when the controller first saw it and until when it counts. Records of entries removed from the spec go. |
| `spec.freeze.exemptionRecords[].firstSeen` | string (date-time) | yes | FirstSeen is when the controller first saw the entry. |
| `spec.freeze.exemptionRecords[].key` | string | yes | Key identifies the entry: a hash of every field, so an edited entry is a new exemption (changewindow.ExemptionKey). |
| `spec.freeze.exemptionRecords[].until` | string (date-time) | yes | Until is when it stops counting. |
| `spec.freeze.exemptions` | []object |  | Exemptions let a pipeline, an environment or one version through the freeze until they expire (kardinal override --freeze). The admission policy admits a new one only in its creator's name, and none changes. |
| `spec.freeze.exemptions[].actor` | object |  | Actor is who made the exception, as the chart's actor admission policy verified it (kardinal override --freeze stamps it). An exemption whose actor is an agent is never honoured: break-glass is for people (docs/design/18-actor-policy.md section 6). |
| `spec.freeze.exemptions[].actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.freeze.exemptions[].actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |

| `spec.freeze.exemptions[].actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `spec.freeze.exemptions[].actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.freeze.exemptions[].actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `spec.freeze.exemptions[].bundle` | string |  | Bundle, when set, limits the exemption to that version. |
