| `spec.environments[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef.eks.region` | string | yes | Region is the cluster's AWS region (its STS endpoint). |
| `spec.environments[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef.eks.roleARN` | string | yes | RoleARN is the IAM role the controller assumes. Its trust policy should require aws:RequestTag/kardinal-namespace (and kardinal-pipeline) to name the Pipelines allowed to use it; it needs eks:DescribeCluster on the cluster, and an EKS access entry maps it to a Kubernetes group bound to read the health objects. |
| `spec.environments[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef.key` | string |  | Key is the key holding the kubeconfig. Defaults to "kubeconfig". |
| `spec.environments[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef.name` | string | yes | Name is the Secret name. |

Example: {"app": "my-service", "kardinal.io/pipeline": "nginx-demo"} Only applies to health.type=resource. Ignored for argocd, flux, argoRollouts, flagger (those resource types are always single-named). |
| `spec.environments[].health.refresh` | boolean |  | Refresh asks the GitOps tool to sync as soon as the promotion's commit is in git, instead of waiting for its poll interval: when health.type (or delivery.delegate) is argocd or flux, or health.refreshTarget names an Application or Kustomization, the step entering HealthChecking sets argocd.argoproj.io/refresh: normal on the Application, or reconcile.fluxcd.io/requestedAt on the Kustomization and its source GitRepository, once (status.refreshRequestedAt). A failed request is not a failure: the tool syncs on its own poll. Default true; false turns it off for this environment. Empty fields default as for health.argocd and health.flux. health.refresh: false turns the refresh off. |

| `spec.environments[].health.refreshTarget.argocd.name` | string |  | Name is the object name. |
| `spec.environments[].health.refreshTarget.argocd.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the object namespace. |
| `spec.environments[].health.refreshTarget.flux` | object |  | Flux is the Kustomization to refresh, with its source GitRepository. Defaults: name "&lt;pipeline&gt;-&lt;environment&gt;", namespace "flux-system". |
| `spec.environments[].health.refreshTarget.flux.name` | string |  | Name is the object name. |
| `spec.environments[].health.refreshTarget.flux.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the object namespace. |

Use this when the health target is in a different namespace or has a different name than the pipeline. Only applies to health.type=resource. Ignored for argocd, flux, argoRollouts, flagger. |
| `spec.environments[].health.resource.condition` | string |  | Condition is the Deployment condition type that must be True. Defaults to "Available". |
| `spec.environments[].health.resource.kind` | string |  | Kind is the Kubernetes resource kind. Only "Deployment" is supported; any other value fails the PromotionStep with a clear message. Defaults to "Deployment" when unset. |
| `spec.environments[].health.resource.name` | string |  | Name is the resource name. Defaults to the pipeline name when unset. |
| `spec.environments[].health.resource.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the resource namespace. Defaults to the environment name when unset. |
| `spec.environments[].health.timeout` | string |  | Timeout is the maximum time to wait for a healthy check: from the start of health checking, and again whenever a bake window stops. | `spec.environments[].health.type` | string |  | Type selects the health check backend. Supported values: resource, argocd, flux, argoRollouts, flagger. When empty the PromotionStep reconciler uses "resource" (a Deployment named after the Pipeline in the environment namespace, unless health.resource overrides it). delivery.delegate, when set, takes precedence. One of: `resource`, `argocd`, `flux`, `argoRollouts`, `flagger`. |
| `spec.environments[].hooks` | []object |  | Hooks are Jobs that run for each Bundle in this environment: "pre" hooks before the promotion starts (database migrations), "post" hooks after the health check passed and before the environment is Verified (integration tests). Each runs once per Bundle, as a HookRun the Bundle's Graph creates. See docs/hooks.md. |
| `spec.environments[].hooks[].job` | object | yes | Job is a batch/v1 JobSpec. The controller creates the Job in the Pipeline namespace with the HookRun as its owner. The Pod's serviceAccountName (default "default") must be in the controller's --hook-service-accounts list. restartPolicy defaults to Never, and activeDeadlineSeconds to the timeout. |
| `spec.environments[].hooks[].name` | string | yes | Name identifies the hook within its environment and phase. It is part of the HookRun and Job names. |
| `spec.environments[].hooks[].phase` | string | yes | Phase is when the hook runs. "pre": after the environment's upstreams are Verified and its gates are ready, before the promotion starts; the promotion starts only when every pre hook succeeded. "post": after the health check passed; the environment is Verified only when every post hook succeeded, and a failed post hook applies onHealthFailure. Hooks of one phase run one after another, in list order. One of: `pre`, `post`. |

See docs/rendered-manifests.md. One of: `directory`, `branch`. Default: `directory`. |

"none" (default): step → Failed; downstream stops. One of: `rollback`, `abort`, `none`. Default: `none`. |
| `spec.environments[].path` | string |  | Path is the subdirectory within the GitOps repository for this environment. Used when spec.git.layout is "directory". Defaults to "environments/&lt;name&gt;". |

| `spec.environments[].pr.merge` | object |  | Merge asks the SCM to merge the PR on its own once the repository's required checks and approvals pass. |

| `spec.environments[].pr.merge.auto` | boolean |  | Auto enables the SCM's auto-merge on the PR once kardinal has opened it (GitHub auto-merge, GitLab auto-merge, Forgejo/Gitea scheduled merge, Azure DevOps auto-complete, Bitbucket Data Center auto-merge): the SCM merges it once the required checks and reviews pass. kardinal turns auto-merge off while the Pipeline is paused or a required gate is closed, and on again after. | `spec.environments[].pr.merge.method` | string |  | Method is how the SCM merges the PR: merge (a merge commit), squash or rebase. Empty uses merge. One of: `merge`, `squash`, `rebase`. |
| `spec.environments[].pr.reviewers` | []string |  | Reviewers are the users asked to review the PR (templates, one user per output line). Usernames on GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo and Gitea; account IDs or {UUID}s on Bitbucket Cloud; identity IDs on Azure DevOps. |
| `spec.environments[].pr.teamReviewers` | []string |  | TeamReviewers are the teams asked to review the PR (templates, one team slug per output line): GitHub and Forgejo/Gitea organisation teams, or group identity IDs on Azure DevOps. |
| `spec.environments[].pr.titleTemplate` | string |  | TitleTemplate replaces the default title "[kardinal] Promote &lt;bundle&gt; to &lt;env&gt;" (or the rollback title). Newlines become spaces; an empty result fails the step. |
| `spec.environments[].render` | object |  | Render configures layout: branch. |
| `spec.environments[].render.allowNondeterministic` | boolean |  | AllowNondeterministic lets Helm templates call functions whose result changes from one render to the next (randAlphaNum, uuidv4, now, genCA and the like). Off by default: such a chart renders different manifests for the same DRY commit, so every promotion commits a change and a rollback does not restore what ran. |
| `spec.environments[].render.branch` | string |  | Branch is the rendered branch the manifests are committed to. Defaults to env/&lt;environment name&gt;. It must differ from spec.git.branch and from every other environment's rendered branch. |
| `spec.environments[].render.helm` | object |  | Helm configures the render of a Helm chart (an environment path holding a Chart.yaml). |
| `spec.environments[].render.helm.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is .Release.Namespace. Defaults to the environment name. |
| `spec.environments[].render.helm.releaseName` | string |  | ReleaseName is .Release.Name. Defaults to the Pipeline name. |
| `spec.environments[].render.helm.valuesFiles` | []string |  | ValuesFiles are values files, relative to the chart directory, applied in order over the chart's values.yaml. Defaults to update.helm.valuesFile when that is set and is not values.yaml. |
| `spec.environments[].render.onDrift` | string |  | OnDrift is what a promotion does when the rendered branch was changed outside kardinal since the last render (a file kardinal wrote was edited or deleted, or a file in its way was added): fail (default) fails the step and changes nothing; overwrite renders over the change. One of: `fail`, `overwrite`. |
| `spec.environments[].stepTimeoutSeconds` | integer |  | StepTimeoutSeconds is the maximum number of seconds a single promotion step (git-clone, kustomize-set-image, open-pr, etc.) may run. | `spec.environments[].update.helm.valuesFile` | string |  | ValuesFile is the name of the values file to update (relative to the environment path). Defaults to "values.yaml". |
| `spec.environments[].update.strategy` | string |  | Strategy selects the manifest update strategy: kustomize (default, kustomization.yaml images), helm (one values key), argocd (patch the Application, no git), or yaml (any YAML paths in any files of the environment directory). | `spec.environments[].update.yaml` | object |  | YAML holds the edits of the yaml strategy. Used when Strategy is "yaml". |
| `spec.environments[].update.yaml.updates` | []object | yes | Updates are the values to set. |

| `spec.environments[].verification.args[].value` | string | yes | Value is the arg value. |
| `spec.environments[].verification.inconclusive` | string |  | Inconclusive is what an Inconclusive AnalysisRun counts as: "fail" (default) or "pass". One of: `fail`, `pass`. |
| `spec.environments[].verification.timeout` | string |  | Timeout bounds the analyses from the moment the environment entered Verifying. An analysis still running then fails the environment. Empty or "0" means 30m. |
| `spec.environments[].waitForMergeTimeout` | string |  | WaitForMergeTimeout is the maximum duration a PromotionStep will wait in the WaitingForMerge state before transitioning to Failed. | `spec.environments[].wave` | integer |  | Wave assigns this environment to a numbered deployment wave. Environments with the same wave number are promoted in parallel. Without DependsOn, a wave also follows the last environment without a wave listed before its first environment, so a wave after "staging" starts once staging is verified, and an environment without a wave follows the environment listed before it, or every environment of that one's wave. DependsOn replaces these list-order edges but never the edges to the previous wave. Only the first listed environment is a root unless DependsOn says otherwise. |
| `spec.git` | object | yes | Git holds the shared GitOps repository configuration for all environments in this pipeline. |
| `spec.git.branch` | string |  | Branch is the base branch: git-clone checks it out, approval: auto pushes to it, and pr-review PRs target it. Defaults to main. Default: `main`. |
| `spec.git.layout` | string |  | Layout controls how environment paths are organized in the repository. "directory": environments as subdirectories on one branch (default). "branch": environments as separate branches. One of: `directory`, `branch`. Default: `directory`. |
| `spec.git.providerRef` | object |  | ProviderRef names the ScmProvider (in the Pipeline's namespace) or the ClusterScmProvider the Pipeline opens its PRs on and reads their state from. Unset uses the controller's --scm-provider. Git clone and push still use secretRef. |
| `spec.git.providerRef.kind` | string |  | Kind is ScmProvider (in the Pipeline's namespace, the default) or ClusterScmProvider. One of: `ScmProvider`, `ClusterScmProvider`. Default: `ScmProvider`. |
| `spec.git.providerRef.name` | string | yes | Name is the provider's name. |
| `spec.git.secretRef` | object |  | SecretRef references a Kubernetes Secret containing the SCM token. |
| `spec.git.secretRef.name` | string | yes | Name is the Secret name. |
| `spec.git.secretRef.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the Secret namespace. If empty, the Pipeline's namespace is used. For spec.git.secretRef it must be empty or equal to the Pipeline's namespace: the controller refuses to read a Secret from another namespace and fails the PromotionStep with a clear message, so a Pipeline author cannot borrow another team's credentials. |
| `spec.git.url` | string | yes | URL is the GitOps repository URL (HTTPS). |
| `spec.historyLimit` | integer |  | HistoryLimit is the number of completed Bundle promotions to retain. When unset or zero, defaults to 50. Terminal Bundles (Verified, Failed, Superseded) beyond this limit are deleted oldest-first on each new Bundle creation. Default: `50`. |
| `spec.holds` | []object |  | Holds pin environments to a rollback (kardinal rollback --hold): while an environment has a hold, no Bundle but the hold's own promotes into it, the hold's Bundle is never superseded or garbage-collected, and, when the controller can verify it restores artifacts Verified in the environment, it passes that environment's PolicyGates, each pass recorded (GateExempted). kardinal unhold removes it, and so does the controller at expiresAt. At most one hold per environment. Changing spec.holds needs update on the virtual subresource pipelines/hold (chart: &lt;release&gt;-hold-writes ValidatingAdmissionPolicy). |
| `spec.holds[].actor` | object |  | Actor is CreatedBy's actor stamp (docs/actors.md), checked by the chart's actor admission policy; the HoldCreated AuditEvent names it. |
| `spec.holds[].actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.holds[].actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |
| `spec.holds[].actor.asserted.client` | string |  | Client is the tool that wrote the record (for example kardinal/0.12.0). |
| `spec.holds[].actor.asserted.model` | string |  | Model is the AI model the client says it runs. |
| `spec.holds[].actor.asserted.session` | string |  | Session is the client's session or run identifier. |
| `spec.holds[].actor.kind` | string | yes | Kind is human, agent, bot or controller (docs/actors.md). One of: `human`, `agent`, `bot`, `controller`. |
| `spec.holds[].actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `spec.holds[].actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.holds[].actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `spec.holds[].artifacts` | string |  | Artifacts is the digest of the rollback Bundle's artifacts (type, images, configRef) when the hold was made (lifecycle.ArtifactDigest). The gate exemption applies only while the Bundle still has them. |
| `spec.holds[].bundle` | string | yes | Bundle is the Bundle the environment is held on (a rollback, or the version running there): the only Bundle that promotes into it while the hold lasts. |
| `spec.holds[].createdAt` | string (date-time) |  | CreatedAt is when. |
| `spec.holds[].createdBy` | string |  | CreatedBy is who held the environment: the Kubernetes user name of the request that added the hold (the admission policy refuses another value), or, for a hold added through the UI, the UI user the controller authenticated. |
| `spec.holds[].environment` | string | yes | Environment is the held environment. |
| `spec.holds[].expiresAt` | string (date-time) |  | ExpiresAt, when set, is when the controller removes the hold. |
| `spec.holds[].reason` | string | yes | Reason says why the environment is held. It is shown wherever the hold or a gate it exempts is. |
| `spec.imageVerification` | object |  | ImageVerification requires the signatures of the Bundle's images (and of a config Bundle's commit) to verify before the Bundle is promoted into its first environments. Selected images must be pinned by digest. See docs/image-verification.md. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations` | []object |  | Attestations are the in-toto attestations each verified image must (or may) carry, as Sigstore bundles in its OCI referrers: SLSA provenance, vulnerability scans with VEX, and any other predicate. Each result is recorded in status.attestations; PolicyGate CEL reads it as attestations.&lt;name&gt; (docs/image-verification.md#attestations). |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].authorities` | []string | yes | Authorities name the spec.imageVerification.authorities that may sign the attestation. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].datedBy` | string |  | DatedBy logTime dates a key-signed attestation whose statement has no time of its own by its transparency log entry or timestamp authority time. Anyone can log an old key signature again or stamp it anew, so such an attestation can be made to look fresh: use it only for an attestation that has no signed time and whose log you trust not to take re-submissions. Empty: such an attestation is stale at once. A keyless attestation needs neither when its certificate lives at most an hour: it is dated by its verified time, which must fall inside the certificate's validity (a Fulcio certificate's ten minutes from signing), so a fresh entry or stamp over an old keyless signature does not verify. One with a longer-lived certificate (a private CA) is dated like a key signature. One of: `logTime`. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].maxAge` | string |  | MaxAge, when set, is how old the attestation may be (a Go duration, for example 24h), from the time its signed statement gives: a scan's scannedAt, a SLSA provenance's finishedOn (buildFinishedOn in v0.2; with both, the earlier), a SLSA verification summary's timeVerified. A keyless attestation without one counts from its verified signing time when its certificate lives at most an hour (Fulcio's: ten minutes), which bounds it. Any other has no time it cannot be re-stamped with, and is stale at once unless datedBy is logTime. Past maxAge the result is stale (status.attestations[].stale, attestations.&lt;name&gt;.stale in a gate), also after the ImageVerification is Verified, and kardinal looks for a newer attestation in the image's referrers until one replaces it. A required attestation that is already stale is waited for like a missing one. See docs/image-verification.md#attestation-age. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].name` | string | yes | Name names the result: a gate reads attestations.&lt;name&gt;. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].predicateType` | string | yes | PredicateType is the in-toto predicate type, exactly ("https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1"). |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].required` | boolean |  | Required holds the version until every image carries a verified attestation of this type, and fails it at the timeout. False records the attestation when it is there. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].slsa` | object |  | SLSA grants SLSA build levels to provenance builders, and holds a version below MinLevel. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].slsa.builders` | []object |  | Builders map trusted builder IDs to the level granted to them. Provenance from a builder not listed is level 1. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].slsa.builders[].id` | string | yes | ID is the builder's runDetails.builder.id, exactly. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].slsa.builders[].level` | integer | yes | Level is the SLSA build level granted (1 to 3). |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].slsa.minLevel` | integer |  | MinLevel holds the version (Failed at the timeout) while an image's level is below it. 0 holds nothing. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].vex` | object |  | VEX names who may say, with OpenVEX statements, that a finding of the scan does not apply. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].vex.authorities` | []string | yes | Authorities name the spec.imageVerification.authorities whose OpenVEX attestations count. A scan's own signer does not suppress its findings unless it is listed here. |
| `spec.imageVerification.attestations[].vex.predicateType` | string |  | PredicateType is the predicate type of the VEX attestations. Empty means https://openvex.dev/ns. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities` | []object |  | Authorities are the signers an image may be signed by: an image is verified when one of its signatures verifies against any authority. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].key` | object |  | Key is a PEM public key (cosign.pub) in a Secret of the Pipeline namespace. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].key.requireTransparencyLog` | boolean |  | RequireTransparencyLog requires a Rekor entry (and its inclusion proof) in the Sigstore bundle. Default false: a key signature is verified against the key alone, like cosign --insecure-ignore-tlog. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].key.secretRef` | object | yes | SecretRef names the Secret and key holding the PEM public key. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].key.secretRef.key` | string | yes | Key is the data key. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].key.secretRef.name` | string | yes | Name is the object name. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].keyless` | object |  | Keyless is a Sigstore keyless identity: the OIDC issuer and subject of the Fulcio certificate that signed. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].keyless.issuer` | string | yes | Issuer is the OIDC issuer, for example https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].keyless.subject` | string |  | Subject is the certificate's subject (SAN), for example https://github.com/myorg/app/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].keyless.subjectRegExp` | string |  | SubjectRegExp is a regular expression the subject must match. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].keyless.trustedRootRef` | object |  | TrustedRootRef names a Secret key in the Pipeline namespace holding a Sigstore trusted_root.json (a private Sigstore). Empty means the Sigstore public-good instance, whose trusted root the controller fetches through TUF. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].keyless.trustedRootRef.key` | string | yes | Key is the data key. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].keyless.trustedRootRef.name` | string | yes | Name is the object name. |
| `spec.imageVerification.authorities[].name` | string | yes | Name identifies the authority in results. |
| `spec.imageVerification.commits` | object |  | Commits, when requireSigned is true, requires the commit of a config or mixed Bundle (spec.configRef.commitSHA) to be signed, as the SCM provider reports it (GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Gitea). |
| `spec.imageVerification.commits.allowedSigners` | []string |  | AllowedSigners, when set, also requires the signer to be one of these: an SCM login or an email address, as the SCM reports the verified signer (GitLab: the key owner's verified email, the committer's for SSH; never a key title). Commits the SCM platform signed itself, not a person, are refused unless listed here explicitly: "web-flow" (GitHub web UI edits and merges), "gitlab-system" (GitLab verified_system) and "forgejo-instance" (the Forgejo/Gitea instance key). To accept PRs merged in the web UI, list the platform identity. Empty means any person's signature the SCM verified. |
| `spec.imageVerification.commits.authorities` | []string |  | Authorities, when set, has kardinal verify the commit's gitsign (Sigstore) signature itself instead of asking the SCM: they name keyless spec.imageVerification.authorities, and the commit verifies when its signature verifies against one of them. The signed payload is read from the SCM API (GitHub, Forgejo, Gitea), the commit SHA is recomputed from it, and the Rekor entry embedded in the signature is checked offline against the authority's trusted root. A GPG or SSH signature is then refused, and allowedSigners does not apply. See docs/image-verification.md#commit-signatures-with-gitsign. |
| `spec.imageVerification.commits.requireSigned` | boolean | yes | RequireSigned requires the config Bundle's commit to be signed with a signature the SCM provider verified. configRef.commitSHA must then be a full 40- or 64-character SHA, and configRef.gitRepo must be on the controller's SCM host. |
| `spec.imageVerification.images` | []string |  | Images selects the Bundle images to verify by repository, with "*" matching any characters ("ghcr.io/myorg/*"). Empty means every image. Every selected image must be pinned by digest in the Bundle. |
| `spec.imageVerification.insecureRegistries` | []string |  | InsecureRegistries are registry hosts ("registry.local:5000") read over plain HTTP. Every other registry is read over HTTPS. |
| `spec.imageVerification.registrySecretRef` | object |  | RegistrySecretRef names a kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret in the Pipeline namespace with credentials for the registries holding the images and their signatures. Without it registries are read anonymously. |
| `spec.imageVerification.registrySecretRef.name` | string | yes | Name is the object name. |
| `spec.imageVerification.signatureRepository` | string |  | SignatureRepository is the repository that holds the signatures, when they are not stored next to the images (cosign's COSIGN_REPOSITORY), for example "registry.example.com/signatures". Signatures are looked up there by image digest. |
| `spec.imageVerification.timeout` | string |  | Timeout bounds how long a missing signature is waited for (CI may sign after it pushes), from the moment the ImageVerification starts. A signature that does not verify fails at once. Empty or "0" means 10m. |
| `spec.lastChange` | object |  | LastChange is who made the latest pause, resume or hold release, and why: kardinal pause, resume and release-hold, and the UI, write it in the same update as the change, and the chart's admission policies admit it only in the requester's name (by, and the actor stamp). The Pipeline reconciler names them in the change's AuditEvent; a change made without it (kubectl) is recorded with an unknown actor. |
| `spec.lastChange.action` | string | yes | Action is the change: Pause, Resume, PauseFleet, ResumeFleet or ReleaseHold. One of: `Pause`, `Resume`, `PauseFleet`, `ResumeFleet`, `ReleaseHold`. |
| `spec.lastChange.actor` | object |  | Actor is By's actor stamp (docs/actors.md), checked by the chart's actor admission policy. |
| `spec.lastChange.actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.lastChange.actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |
| `spec.lastChange.actor.asserted.client` | string |  | Client is the tool that wrote the record (for example kardinal/0.12.0). |
| `spec.lastChange.actor.asserted.model` | string |  | Model is the AI model the client says it runs. |
| `spec.lastChange.actor.asserted.session` | string |  | Session is the client's session or run identifier. |
| `spec.lastChange.actor.kind` | string | yes | Kind is human, agent, bot or controller (docs/actors.md). One of: `human`, `agent`, `bot`, `controller`. |
| `spec.lastChange.actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `spec.lastChange.actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `spec.lastChange.actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `spec.lastChange.by` | string | yes | By is the requester's username, as the API server authenticated it. |
| `spec.lastChange.id` | string |  | ID is set anew by each write (a random id), so the same person making the same change twice writes two records: the Pipeline reconciler uses each record once (status.observedLastChange). |
| `spec.lastChange.reason` | string |  | Reason says why (kardinal pause --reason). |
| `spec.lastChange.target` | string |  | Target is the fleet (PauseFleet, ResumeFleet) or the held environment (ReleaseHold); empty for the Pipeline. |
| `spec.maxConcurrentPromotions` | integer |  | MaxConcurrentPromotions caps the number of Bundles in Promoting phase for this pipeline at any given time. When 0 or unset (default), there is no cap and all Available Bundles are promoted concurrently. When set to a positive value, Bundles that exceed the cap are requeued until a promotion slot becomes available. This prevents promotion storms (e.g. a CI burst creating 50 Bundles simultaneously) from saturating git hosts, exhausting GitHub API rate limits, or creating merge conflicts in the GitOps repository. Example: maxConcurrentPromotions: 2 allows at most 2 active promotions at once. Additional Available Bundles wait in a 30-second polling loop. Default: `0`. |
| `spec.paused` | boolean |  | Paused suspends all promotions in this pipeline when true. Default: `false`. |
| `spec.pausedFleets` | []string |  | PausedFleets pauses fleet environments (kardinal pause &lt;pipeline&gt; --env &lt;fleet&gt;): no further target of a listed fleet starts, for any Bundle, and the targets in flight finish, as when maxUnavailable is reached. Each entry names an environment with a fleet; another name makes the Pipeline Ready=False (ValidationFailed). Changing spec.pausedFleets needs update on the virtual subresource pipelines/pause, as spec.paused does. |
| `spec.policyNamespaces` | []string |  | PolicyNamespaces lists extra namespaces to read PolicyGates from. It only adds to the list: the controller's org policy namespaces (--policy-namespaces, default "platform-policies") and the pipeline's own namespace are always read, so a Pipeline cannot opt out of org gates. Gates found only through this field are team gates: they never count as org gates and never grant a skip. Any other namespace listed must agree to be read: the label kardinal.io/policy-shareable=true on it, or the controller's --policy-shareable-namespaces. One that has not is still read for now, and the Pipeline's PolicyNamespacesShared condition is False naming it; a later release refuses it. |
| `status` | object |  | PipelineStatus defines the observed state of a Pipeline. |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | Conditions holds status conditions. |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status.conditions[].status` | string | yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. One of: `True`, `False`, `Unknown`. |
| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics` | object |  | DeploymentMetrics holds aggregate DORA-style metrics computed from the last 30 Verified Bundles for this Pipeline. Written by PipelineReconciler. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.autoRollbackRateMillis` | integer |  | AutoRollbackRateMillis is the fraction of sampled Bundles that are rollbacks the controller started on its own (onHealthFailure: rollback, a RollbackPolicy: label kardinal.io/reason=AutoRollback), expressed as integer thousandths (e.g. 83 = 8.3%). Rollbacks a person started (`kardinal rollback`, the UI) count in RollbackRateMillis only. Stored as integer to avoid floating-point in CRD YAML. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.changeFailureRateMillis` | integer |  | ChangeFailureRateMillis is failedDeployments / deployments as integer thousandths (DORA change failure rate; 250 = 25%). |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.computedAt` | string (date-time) |  | ComputedAt is when these metrics were last written by the PipelineReconciler. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.deployments` | integer |  | Deployments is the number of deployments the change failure rate and time to restore are computed over: the last 30 Bundles whose change reached a final environment (one nothing depends on; its health check started), whatever the outcome, once per Bundle. Not deployments: a no-op promotion (outputs.noChanges), the steps a supersession cancelled (a RollingBack, AbortedByAlarm or already Failed step of a superseded Bundle still counts), and rollback Bundles (they count only as restores). |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.failedDeployments` | integer |  | FailedDeployments is how many of those deployments failed: a PromotionStep in a final environment ended Failed, AbortedByAlarm or RollingBack after its health check started, a rollback Bundle later rolled a final environment back from it (annotation kardinal.io/rollback-from), or the Bundle was rejected after it was deployed. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.leadTimeFromCommit` | integer |  | LeadTimeFromCommit is how many of the sampled Bundles' lead times start at spec.provenance.commitTime; the others start at the Bundle's creation. Rollback Bundles have no lead time and are not counted. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.meanTimeToRestoreMinutes` | integer (int64) |  | MeanTimeToRestoreMinutes is the mean, in whole minutes, from each failed deployment reaching a final environment to the first later Bundle Verified in every final environment it targets, in every region (DORA time to restore). Failures not restored yet are not counted. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.operatorInterventionRateMillis` | integer |  | OperatorInterventionRateMillis is the fraction of sampled Bundles that had at least one PolicyGate override applied, expressed as integer thousandths. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.p50CommitToProdMinutes` | integer (int64) |  | P50CommitToProdMinutes is the median time (minutes) from the commit to the final environment reaching Verified, over the sample window. A Bundle's commit time is spec.provenance.commitTime when CI set it; otherwise the Bundle's creation, which leaves out the build (LeadTimeFromCommit counts the Bundles measured from the commit). Rollback Bundles are left out: they restore a change, they do not ship one. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.p90CommitToProdMinutes` | integer (int64) |  | P90CommitToProdMinutes is the 90th-percentile time (minutes) from the commit (as for P50CommitToProdMinutes) to the final environment reaching Verified, over the sample window. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.restoredFailures` | integer |  | RestoredFailures is the number of failed deployments in meanTimeToRestoreMinutes. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.rollbackRateMillis` | integer |  | RollbackRateMillis is the fraction of sampled Bundles that are rollbacks of any kind (spec.provenance.rollbackOf is set): automatic or started by a person, in integer thousandths. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.rolloutsLast30Days` | integer |  | RolloutsLast30Days is the number of successful (Verified) promotions to the final pipeline environment in the last 30 calendar days. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.sampleSize` | integer |  | SampleSize is the number of Bundles included in this computation. |
| `status.deploymentMetrics.staleProdDays` | integer |  | StaleProdDays is the number of days since the last successful promotion to the final pipeline environment. 0 means a promotion completed today. Until a Bundle is Verified there, deploymentMetrics is not set at all. |
| `status.environmentSummary` | string |  | EnvironmentSummary is Environments as one line, environment=version ("test=1.5.0 uat=1.5.0 prod=1.4.0"; "-" where nothing runs yet), for the wide printer column. Display only. |
| `status.environments` | []object |  | Environments is, per environment in spec order (a fleet environment expands to its targets), what runs there and where the newest version stands. Written by the PipelineReconciler from the Bundles, PromotionSteps and gate instances of the Pipeline. It is a display projection: no controller decision reads it. |
| `status.environments[].blockedBy` | []string |  | BlockedBy names the gates that hold the newest Bundle back in the environment, sorted. |
| `status.environments[].bundle` | string |  | Bundle is the Bundle whose change runs in the environment: the newest one whose change landed there. Empty when none has. |
| `status.environments[].frozenBy` | string |  | FrozenBy is the freeze (ChangeWindow name) that holds the newest Bundle's step here: its PromotionStep's status.frozenBy. |
| `status.environments[].held` | boolean |  | Held is true when a rollback hold (spec.holds) keeps the environment on Bundle, so the newest Bundle waits. |
| `status.environments[].incomingBundle` | string |  | IncomingBundle is a newer Bundle on its way into the environment (its step there is not yet live, or gates hold it before its step exists). Empty when the newest Bundle there is Bundle. |
| `status.environments[].incomingVersion` | string |  | IncomingVersion is what IncomingBundle ships. |
| `status.environments[].name` | string | yes | Name is the environment name. |
| `status.environments[].prURL` | string |  | PRURL is the pull request of the newest Bundle's step while it waits for its merge. |
| `status.environments[].receipts` | object |  | Receipts counts the environment's promotion receipts and their size, when receipts are enabled (docs/receipts.md): what retention would have to delete, and what verify-receipt --image reads per image. |
| `status.environments[].receipts.bytes` | integer (int64) | yes | Bytes is their total size (statements and signed bundles). |
| `status.environments[].receipts.count` | integer (int64) | yes | Count is how many PromotionReceipts the environment has. |
| `status.environments[].since` | string (date-time) |  | Since is when State began: the Verified time for Verified, otherwise when the controller first recorded this Bundle in this State. |
| `status.environments[].state` | string |  | State is the PromotionStep state of the newest Bundle in the environment (IncomingBundle when set, else Bundle), an API value such as Verified or WaitingForMerge. Pending with BlockedBy set when gates hold the Bundle before its step exists. Empty when no Bundle reached the environment. |
| `status.environments[].version` | string |  | Version is what Bundle ships: the image tag, "config &lt;sha&gt;" or the chart version. |
| `status.failedVersion` | object |  | FailedVersion is the newest version of the Pipeline when it failed: its Bundle is the newest of the Pipeline and is Failed, before any step (the Graph could not be built, the spec is invalid) or in an environment. Cleared once a newer Bundle exists. Written with Environments from the Bundle's conditions; display only, so the CLI (why, status) and the UI can say why without reading the Bundle. |
| `status.failedVersion.bundle` | string | yes | Bundle is the failed Bundle. |
| `status.failedVersion.environment` | string |  | Environment is the environment whose step failed; empty when the Bundle failed before any step. |
| `status.failedVersion.message` | string |  | Message is that condition's message: what failed and, where known, what fixes it. |
| `status.failedVersion.reason` | string | yes | Reason is the reason of the Bundle's InvalidSpec condition (GraphBuildFailed, InvalidIntent, InvalidPipeline, ...) or of its Failed condition. |
| `status.failedVersion.since` | string (date-time) |  | Since is when the Bundle failed (its Ready condition's transition). |
| `status.failedVersion.version` | string |  | Version is what Bundle ships (the image tag, "config &lt;sha&gt;" or the chart version). |
| `status.fleets` | []object |  | Fleets are the resolved targets of each fleet environment that uses a selector, written by the PipelineReconciler. A Bundle's Graph is built from them; a change rebuilds the Graph of a Bundle in flight. |
| `status.fleets[].environment` | string | yes | Environment is the fleet environment. |
| `status.fleets[].message` | string |  | Message says why the selector could not be resolved, when it could not. |
| `status.fleets[].targets` | []object |  | Targets are the selected Applications as targets, sorted by name. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health` | object |  | Health replaces the environment's health check for this target. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.argoRollouts` | object |  | ArgoRollouts overrides the Rollout checked by health.type=argoRollouts (or delivery.delegate=argoRollouts). Defaults: name "&lt;pipeline&gt;", namespace "&lt;environment&gt;". |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.argoRollouts.name` | string |  | Name is the object name. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.argoRollouts.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the object namespace. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.argocd` | object |  | ArgoCD overrides the Argo CD Application checked by health.type=argocd. Defaults: name "&lt;pipeline&gt;-&lt;environment&gt;", namespace "argocd". |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.argocd.name` | string |  | Name is the object name. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.argocd.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the object namespace. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.flagger` | object |  | Flagger overrides the Canary checked by health.type=flagger (or delivery.delegate=flagger). Defaults: name "&lt;pipeline&gt;", namespace "&lt;environment&gt;". |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.flagger.name` | string |  | Name is the object name. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.flagger.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the object namespace. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.flux` | object |  | Flux overrides the Flux Kustomization checked by health.type=flux. Defaults: name "&lt;pipeline&gt;-&lt;environment&gt;", namespace "flux-system". |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.flux.name` | string |  | Name is the object name. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.flux.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the object namespace. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef` | object |  | KubeconfigSecretRef runs the health check against another cluster: the one the kubeconfig in this Secret key selects (its current context). The Secret must be in the Pipeline's namespace. Every health type reads its object (Deployment, Application, Kustomization, Rollout, Canary) in that cluster instead of the controller's. Only inline credentials are accepted: a bearer token, a client certificate and key (-data fields), or a username and password. A kubeconfig with exec, auth-provider, tokenFile or any file path is refused and the step fails: it would run a command, or read a file, in the controller. The API server address goes through the controller's egress guard (no loopback, link-local or metadata addresses) and is dialled directly, not through HTTP(S)_PROXY. A cluster that cannot be reached is not unhealthy: the step reports ClusterUnreachable and keeps checking until health.timeout. Remote health is polled, not watched. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef.eks` | object |  | EKS authenticates to an Amazon EKS cluster with the controller's own AWS identity (IRSA or EKS Pod Identity) instead of a credential in the kubeconfig. The controller assumes RoleARN, with the session tags kardinal-namespace and kardinal-pipeline set to this Pipeline's namespace and name, reads the cluster's endpoint and CA with eks:DescribeCluster as that role, and sends a 15-minute EKS token for ClusterName, signed as the role (as aws-iam-authenticator does), to that endpoint only; no long-lived secret exists. The Secret's kubeconfig is then optional and may hold no users[].user credentials; a server it names must be the cluster's endpoint. RoleARN must match the controller's --health-eks-role-arns or, for this namespace, --health-eks-role-arns-by-namespace (Helm health.eks), both empty, so the feature is off, by default (docs/health-adapters.md, Remote clusters on EKS). |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef.eks.clusterName` | string | yes | ClusterName is the EKS cluster's name, the x-k8s-aws-id the token is signed for. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef.eks.region` | string | yes | Region is the cluster's AWS region (its STS endpoint). |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef.eks.roleARN` | string | yes | RoleARN is the IAM role the controller assumes. Its trust policy should require aws:RequestTag/kardinal-namespace (and kardinal-pipeline) to name the Pipelines allowed to use it; it needs eks:DescribeCluster on the cluster, and an EKS access entry maps it to a Kubernetes group bound to read the health objects. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef.key` | string |  | Key is the key holding the kubeconfig. Defaults to "kubeconfig". |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef.name` | string | yes | Name is the Secret name. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.labelSelector` | map[string]string |  | LabelSelector, for health.type=resource, checks every Deployment in the environment namespace that matches these labels instead of one named Deployment: the environment is healthy when all of them are, and unhealthy when none matches. Example: {"app": "my-service", "kardinal.io/pipeline": "nginx-demo"} Only applies to health.type=resource. Ignored for argocd, flux, argoRollouts, flagger (those resource types are always single-named). |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.refresh` | boolean |  | Refresh asks the GitOps tool to sync as soon as the promotion's commit is in git, instead of waiting for its poll interval: when health.type (or delivery.delegate) is argocd or flux, or health.refreshTarget names an Application or Kustomization, the step entering HealthChecking sets argocd.argoproj.io/refresh: normal on the Application, or reconcile.fluxcd.io/requestedAt on the Kustomization and its source GitRepository, once (status.refreshRequestedAt). A failed request is not a failure: the tool syncs on its own poll. Default true; false turns it off for this environment. The controller's --health-refresh=false (Helm health.refresh.enabled) turns it off everywhere. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.refreshTarget` | object |  | RefreshTarget names the GitOps object health.refresh asks to sync when it is not the one the health check reads: the Argo CD Application or Flux Kustomization that deploys the environment, when health.type is argoRollouts, flagger or resource, or when the health check reads another cluster (health.kubeconfigSecretRef) and the GitOps tool runs in the controller's. The object is always in the controller's cluster and is refreshed with the controller's identity, so it must be in the Pipeline's namespace or deploy there, or be admitted by --health-refresh-namespaces. Empty fields default as for health.argocd and health.flux. health.refresh: false turns the refresh off. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.refreshTarget.argocd` | object |  | ArgoCD is the Application to refresh. Defaults: name "&lt;pipeline&gt;-&lt;environment&gt;", namespace "argocd". |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.refreshTarget.argocd.name` | string |  | Name is the object name. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.refreshTarget.argocd.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the object namespace. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.refreshTarget.flux` | object |  | Flux is the Kustomization to refresh, with its source GitRepository. Defaults: name "&lt;pipeline&gt;-&lt;environment&gt;", namespace "flux-system". |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.refreshTarget.flux.name` | string |  | Name is the object name. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.refreshTarget.flux.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the object namespace. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.resource` | object |  | Resource specifies the exact Kubernetes resource to watch for health.type=resource. When set, overrides the default behavior (which watches a Deployment named after the pipeline in the environment namespace). Use this when the health target is in a different namespace or has a different name than the pipeline. Only applies to health.type=resource. Ignored for argocd, flux, argoRollouts, flagger. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.resource.condition` | string |  | Condition is the Deployment condition type that must be True. Defaults to "Available". |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.resource.kind` | string |  | Kind is the Kubernetes resource kind. Only "Deployment" is supported; any other value fails the PromotionStep with a clear message. Defaults to "Deployment" when unset. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.resource.name` | string |  | Name is the resource name. Defaults to the pipeline name when unset. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.resource.namespace` | string |  | Namespace is the resource namespace. Defaults to the environment name when unset. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.timeout` | string |  | Timeout is the maximum time to wait for a healthy check: from the start of health checking, and again whenever a bake window stops. When it expires, onHealthFailure applies. It does not cut a running bake window short. Uses Go duration format (e.g. "30m", "1h"). Defaults to "10m". |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].health.type` | string |  | Type selects the health check backend. Supported values: resource, argocd, flux, argoRollouts, flagger. When empty the PromotionStep reconciler uses "resource" (a Deployment named after the Pipeline in the environment namespace, unless health.resource overrides it). delivery.delegate, when set, takes precedence. One of: `resource`, `argocd`, `flux`, `argoRollouts`, `flagger`. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].labels` | map[string]string |  | Labels describe the target (region, tier, cluster); a selector of kind Target picks targets by them. The labels of a selected Application or ClusterProfile are its own. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].name` | string | yes | Name identifies the target. The target's environment is named "&lt;environment&gt;-&lt;name&gt;", which must be a DNS label of at most 63 characters. |
| `status.fleets[].targets[].path` | string |  | Path is the target's directory in the GitOps repo. Default: the environment's path (default environments/&lt;environment&gt;) followed by "/&lt;name&gt;". |
| `status.holdStates` | []object |  | HoldStates says, per hold of spec.holds, whether its rollback Bundle exists. A hold whose Bundle is missing (a crash between the hold and the Bundle create, or the Bundle deleted) stays in effect; past the grace the controller reports it, and a human releases it. |
| `status.holdStates[].bundle` | string | yes | Bundle is the hold's Bundle the state was found for. |
| `status.holdStates[].bundleMissingSince` | string (date-time) |  | BundleMissingSince is when the controller first found the Bundle missing: the grace counts from it, not from the client-set createdAt. |
| `status.holdStates[].createdAt` | string (date-time) |  | CreatedAt is the hold's createdAt: with the environment and the Bundle it identifies the hold, so a hold released and added again gets a state, and a report, of its own. |
| `status.holdStates[].environment` | string | yes | Environment is the held environment. |
| `status.holdStates[].message` | string |  | Message says what is wrong and how to recover. |
| `status.holdStates[].reportedAt` | string (date-time) |  | ReportedAt is when the controller reported the missing Bundle, once, past the grace. |
| `status.holdStates[].state` | string | yes | State is Active or BundleMissing. |
| `status.observedHolds` | []object |  | ObservedHolds is spec.holds as the Pipeline reconciler last recorded it: the HoldCreated and HoldReleased AuditEvents are written from the difference, whichever client changed spec.holds. |
| `status.observedHolds[].actor` | object |  | Actor is CreatedBy's actor stamp (docs/actors.md), checked by the chart's actor admission policy; the HoldCreated AuditEvent names it. |
| `status.observedHolds[].actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `status.observedHolds[].actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |
| `status.observedHolds[].actor.asserted.client` | string |  | Client is the tool that wrote the record (for example kardinal/0.12.0). |
| `status.observedHolds[].actor.asserted.model` | string |  | Model is the AI model the client says it runs. |
| `status.observedHolds[].actor.asserted.session` | string |  | Session is the client's session or run identifier. |
| `status.observedHolds[].actor.kind` | string | yes | Kind is human, agent, bot or controller (docs/actors.md). One of: `human`, `agent`, `bot`, `controller`. |
| `status.observedHolds[].actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `status.observedHolds[].actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `status.observedHolds[].actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `status.observedHolds[].artifacts` | string |  | Artifacts is the digest of the rollback Bundle's artifacts (type, images, configRef) when the hold was made (lifecycle.ArtifactDigest). The gate exemption applies only while the Bundle still has them. |
| `status.observedHolds[].bundle` | string | yes | Bundle is the Bundle the environment is held on (a rollback, or the version running there): the only Bundle that promotes into it while the hold lasts. |
| `status.observedHolds[].createdAt` | string (date-time) |  | CreatedAt is when. |
| `status.observedHolds[].createdBy` | string |  | CreatedBy is who held the environment: the Kubernetes user name of the request that added the hold (the admission policy refuses another value), or, for a hold added through the UI, the UI user the controller authenticated. |
| `status.observedHolds[].environment` | string | yes | Environment is the held environment. |
| `status.observedHolds[].expiresAt` | string (date-time) |  | ExpiresAt, when set, is when the controller removes the hold. |
| `status.observedHolds[].reason` | string | yes | Reason says why the environment is held. It is shown wherever the hold or a gate it exempts is. |
| `status.observedLastChange` | string |  | ObservedLastChange identifies the spec.lastChange the Pipeline reconciler last consumed (a hash): a record names who made the change it was written with, and a later change made without one (kubectl) is recorded with no actor, not with the earlier record's. |
| `status.observedPaused` | boolean |  | ObservedPaused is spec.paused as the Pipeline reconciler last recorded it: the PipelinePaused and PipelineResumed AuditEvents are written from the difference, whichever client changed it. Unset until the first record (an upgrade records the current state, unaudited). |
| `status.observedPausedFleets` | []string |  | ObservedPausedFleets is spec.pausedFleets as last recorded, for the AuditEvents of a fleet's pause and resume. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents` | []object |  | PendingAuditEvents are the HoldCreated, HoldReleased and HoldBundleMissing AuditEvents not yet written (the audit outbox). Each entry is stored in the same status patch as observedHolds and removed once the AuditEvent exists. Normally empty. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].createdAt` | string |  | CreatedAt is the transition time in RFC 3339 with nanoseconds, written to the AuditEvent's kardinal.io/created-at annotation: spec.timestamp has one-second resolution. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].labels` | map[string]string |  | Labels are the AuditEvent's labels. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].name` | string | yes | Name is the AuditEvent's name. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec` | object | yes | Spec is the AuditEvent's spec, timestamp included: the record carries the time of the transition, not the time it was written. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.action` | string | yes | Action is a short verb describing what happened. Valid values: "PromotionStarted", "PromotionSucceeded", "PromotionFailed", "PromotionSuperseded", "PromotionRejected", "RollbackStarted", "RollbackSucceeded", "HealthCheckFailed", "GateBlocked", "GateEvaluated", "GateOverridden", "ApprovalRecorded", "ApprovalRevoked", "HoldCreated", "HoldReleased", "HoldBundleMissing", "BundleRejected", "APIWrite", "VerdictRecorded", "VerdictRevoked", "FreezeExempted", "PipelinePaused", "PipelineResumed", "FreezeStarted", "FreezeLifted", "PRMerged", "ReceiptFailed", "ChangeRequestOpened", "ChangeRequestLinked", "ChangeRequestApproved", "ChangeRequestRejected", "GateChanged". The ChangeRequest actions are written by a per-promotion ChangeRequest when it opens or links its ticket, and when the ticket is first read approved or rejected (docs/design/23-change-requests.md section 9). ReceiptFailed is written by a promotion step that reached Verified without a PromotionReceipt, because its receipt could not be built (status.receiptError). PRMerged is written by a promotion step when its pull request is merged, naming who merged it as the SCM API reports it. ApprovalRecorded and ApprovalRevoked are written by an approval gate when a decision (kardinal approve) appears in or leaves its spec.approvals. BundleRejected is written once when a Bundle's spec.rejected is set (kardinal reject or the UI), naming who rejected it and why; its environment is "*" (the whole Bundle). GateOverridden is written once per spec.overrides entry of a gate instance, naming who created it (kardinal override or the UI). APIWrite is written for each write through the UI API or the Bundle API (controller.accessLog.auditEvents), naming the caller in actor and the route in request. FreezeExempted is written once per exemption when a PromotionStep goes on through an active freeze under it (kardinal override --freeze), naming who made the exemption and why. GateChanged is written by the BundleReconciler when a PolicyGate template that applies to a Promoting version was created, edited or deleted and the version's Graph got the change; gates lists the templates of that rebuild with their old and new digest, one event per version and rebuild (#2144). HealthCheckFailed and GateBlocked are accepted but never written: a failed health check records PromotionFailed (RollbackStarted when onHealthFailure is rollback), and a blocked gate records GateEvaluated with outcome Failure. One of: `PromotionStarted`, `PromotionSucceeded`, `PromotionFailed`, `PromotionSuperseded`, `PromotionRejected`, `RollbackStarted`, `RollbackSucceeded`, `HealthCheckFailed`, `GateBlocked`, `GateEvaluated`, `GateOverridden`, `ApprovalRecorded`, `ApprovalRevoked`, `HoldCreated`, `HoldReleased`, `HoldBundleMissing`, `BundleRejected`, `APIWrite`, `VerdictRecorded`, `VerdictRevoked`, `FreezeExempted`, `PipelinePaused`, `PipelineResumed`, `FreezeStarted`, `FreezeLifted`, `PRMerged`, `ReceiptFailed`, `ChangeRequestOpened`, `ChangeRequestLinked`, `ChangeRequestApproved`, `ChangeRequestRejected`, `GateChanged`. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor` | object |  | Actor is who caused the event (docs/actors.md). Absent on records written before v0.12. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.agent` | string |  | Agent is the AgentIdentity name, when kind is agent. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.asserted` | object |  | Asserted holds what the client says about itself. It is recorded as written and never used for a security decision. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.asserted.client` | string |  | Client is the tool that wrote the record (for example kardinal/0.12.0). |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.asserted.model` | string |  | Model is the AI model the client says it runs. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.asserted.session` | string |  | Session is the client's session or run identifier. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.kind` | string | yes | Kind is human, agent, bot or controller (docs/actors.md). One of: `human`, `agent`, `bot`, `controller`. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.principal` | string | yes | Principal is the username the API server authenticated. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.sponsor` | string |  | Sponsor is the agent's sponsor (AgentIdentity spec.sponsor.user) when the record was written, when kind is agent. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.actor.via` | string |  | Via says how the controller came to write the record: ui and api for a caller it authenticated, subscription and auto-rollback for its own Bundles. Only the controller may set it. One of: `ui`, `api`, `subscription`, `auto-rollback`. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.bundleName` | string |  | BundleName is the name of the Bundle being promoted. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.environment` | string |  | Environment is the environment name where the event occurred. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.fields` | map[string]string |  | Fields are an ApprovalRecorded or ApprovalRevoked decision's structured values (Approval spec.fields) the gate declares, whole. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates` | []object |  | Gates are the PolicyGate template changes a GateChanged event records: one event per version and rebuild, listing at most MaxAuditGateChanges changes in template order. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].environmentsAdded` | []string |  | EnvironmentsAdded are environments of the version the template's gate copies now apply to and did not before (a kardinal.io/applies-to edit moves a gate without changing its rule): the first 5 in name order. A record merged from several gives the net move: an environment in environmentsAdded only ends on, one in environmentsRemoved only ends off, and one in both moved and ended where it started. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].environmentsOmitted` | integer (int32) |  | EnvironmentsOmitted is one count, for environmentsAdded and environmentsRemoved together, of the environments past the first 5 of each. In a record merged from several it is an upper bound. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].environmentsRemoved` | []string |  | EnvironmentsRemoved are environments of the version the template's gate copies applied to and no longer do: the first 5 in name order. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].manager` | string |  | Manager is the field manager of the template's newest managedFields entry, as the writing client declared it (kubectl --field-manager sets any name). It is not verified and does not say who wrote the template: the API server's audit log does. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].namespace` | string | yes | Namespace is the template's namespace. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].newDigest` | string |  | NewDigest is the digest the instances have now. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].newGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | NewGeneration is the template generation the instances have now. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].oldDigest` | string |  | OldDigest is the digest the instances had. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].oldGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | OldGeneration is the template generation the instances had. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gates[].template` | string | yes | Template is the PolicyGate template's name. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.gatesOmitted` | integer (int32) |  | GatesOmitted counts the changes of the same rebuild that Gates leaves out, past its first MaxAuditGateChanges. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.mergedRecords` | integer (int32) |  | MergedRecords is how many unwritten records this one replaces: a full audit outbox merges records of the same kind (GateChanged) before it drops any, during an AuditEvent write outage. Absent for a record written as it was recorded. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.message` | string |  | Message is a human-readable description of the event. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.outcome` | string | yes | Outcome describes the result of the action. Valid values: "Success", "Failure", "Pending". One of: `Success`, `Failure`, `Pending`. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.pipelineName` | string |  | PipelineName is the name of the Pipeline the Bundle is promoting through. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.request` | object |  | Request is the API request of an APIWrite event. It records no body and no token. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.request.method` | string | yes | Method is the HTTP method. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.request.route` | string | yes | Route is the API route pattern, for example /api/v1/ui/pipelines/{name}/pause. |
| `status.pendingAuditEvents[].spec.timestamp` | string (date-time) | yes | Timestamp is when the event occurred (RFC 3339 format). |
| `status.phase` | string |  | Phase is the overall pipeline phase: Promoting while a Bundle is in flight (also when a PolicyGate holds it), Degraded when the newest Bundle failed, Ready when the newest Bundle is Verified in every environment it reached, and Unknown before the first Bundle. One of: `Ready`, `Degraded`, `Promoting`, `Unknown`. Default: `Unknown`. |
| `status.summary` | string |  | Summary is one sentence on where the Pipeline's versions are, for example "1.5.0 live in test, uat; waiting for PR merge in prod (#42)". Written with Environments; display only. |

## PolicyGate

`kardinal.io/v1alpha1`

PolicyGate is a CEL-powered policy check represented as a node in the promotion Graph. Platform teams define org-level gates; teams add their own. A gate's name must be at most 63 characters, because the Graph copies it into a label of each instance. Only the PolicyGates kardinal creates may be longer: gate instances ("&lt;gate&gt;-&lt;namespace&gt;-&lt;env&gt;--&lt;bundle&gt;", see pkg/graph gateNodeK8sName) and pause freeze gates ("freeze-&lt;pipeline&gt;"). Kardinal sets spec.generated on them and never uses a gate with spec.generated as a template. The exemption does not go by name, because a template can have any name; a template that sets spec.generated is no longer a template.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | PolicyGateSpec defines the desired state of a PolicyGate. |
| `spec.approval` | object |  | Approval makes the gate wait for people: it is ready only when its expression is true and at least approval.required allowed people have approved the Bundle for the environment (kardinal approve), and none of them rejected it. Copied from the template to every gate instance. For a gate that only waits for approvals, use the expression "true". |
| `spec.approval.allowAgents` | boolean |  | AllowAgents opts the gate in to approvals by agents. An approval whose actor is an agent counts only when this is true and the agent is in allowedAgents, and never on a version of the agent's own party (the agent, its sponsor, or the sponsor's other agents), whatever excludeAuthor says. allowedUsers and allowedGroups do not apply to agents. |
| `spec.approval.allowedAgents` | []string |  | AllowedAgents are the AgentIdentity names whose approvals count when allowAgents is true. |
| `spec.approval.allowedGroups` | []string |  | AllowedGroups are Kubernetes groups: an approval counts when one of the approval's groups is listed. With neither allowedUsers nor allowedGroups, every approval counts; who may approve is then decided by RBAC on approvals. |
| `spec.approval.allowedUsers` | []string |  | AllowedUsers are Kubernetes usernames whose approvals count. |
| `spec.approval.excludeAuthor` | boolean |  | ExcludeAuthor does not count an approval whose user created the Bundle (no self-approval): the kardinal.io/created-by annotation, which the chart's admission policy pins to the creating user (kardinal create bundle, the Bundle API and the UI set it). A Bundle without it blocks the gate: the rule cannot be enforced. It applies the one-party rule: with an actor stamp on the Bundle, an agent's version cannot be approved by the agent, its sponsor or another agent of that sponsor, and a person's version not by the person's own agents. |

Valid values: "PromotionStarted", "PromotionSucceeded", "PromotionFailed", "PromotionSuperseded", "PromotionRejected", "RollbackStarted", "RollbackSucceeded", "HealthCheckFailed", "GateBlocked", "GateEvaluated", "GateOverridden", "ApprovalRecorded", "ApprovalRevoked", "HoldCreated", "HoldReleased", "HoldBundleMissing", "BundleRejected", "APIWrite", "VerdictRecorded", "VerdictRevoked", "FreezeExempted", "PipelinePaused", "PipelineResumed", "FreezeStarted", "FreezeLifted", "PRMerged", "ReceiptFailed", "ChangeRequestOpened", "ChangeRequestLinked", "ChangeRequestApproved", "ChangeRequestRejected", "GateChanged". The ChangeRequest actions are written by a per-promotion ChangeRequest when it opens or links its ticket, and when the ticket is first read approved or rejected (docs/design/23-change-requests.md section 9). ReceiptFailed is written by a promotion step that reached Verified without a PromotionReceipt, because its receipt could not be built (status.receiptError). PRMerged is written by a promotion step when its pull request is merged, naming who merged it as the SCM API reports it. ApprovalRecorded and ApprovalRevoked are written by an approval gate when a decision (kardinal approve) appears in or leaves its spec.approvals. BundleRejected is written once when a Bundle's spec.rejected is set (kardinal reject or the UI), naming who rejected it and why; its environment is "*" (the whole Bundle). GateOverridden is written once per spec.overrides entry of a gate instance, naming who created it (kardinal override or the UI). APIWrite is written for each write through the UI API or the Bundle API (controller.accessLog.auditEvents), naming the caller in actor and the route in request. GateChanged is written by the BundleReconciler when a PolicyGate template that applies to a Promoting version was created, edited or deleted and the version's Graph got the change; gates lists the templates of that rebuild with their old and new digest, one event per version and rebuild (#2144). HealthCheckFailed and GateBlocked are accepted but never written: a failed health check records PromotionFailed (RollbackStarted when onHealthFailure is rollback), and a blocked gate records GateEvaluated with outcome Failure.
